paragraphs: BCG Report Projects Gaming Industry Revenues Will Hit $350 Billion by 2030 Cloud Gaming Revenue Will Reach $18.3 Billion by 2030, Up 57% from 2023 40% of Gamers Are Consuming More User-Generated Content Than Last Year BOSTON —The gaming industry is emerging from its post-pandemic slowdown, with global gaming revenue projected to grow by 6% from 2026 to 2030 and reach $350 billion by 2030.
AI can boost efficiency by improving code and automating quality assurance.
A new survey of approximately 3,000 gamers found that 55% of them increased their playing time during the past six months.
UGC has emerged as a rapidly growing creator economy, with payouts that will reach $1.5 billion in 2025 from two games alone.
More than 40% of survey respondents said that they’re consuming more UGC this year than last year, but only 10% to 15% have created content themselves.
Although 60% of respondents said they had tried cloud gaming, and 80% reported a positive experience, only 27% of gamers said they are regular or heavy users of cloud gaming.
Still, cloud gaming revenues are set to grow from around $1.4 billion in 2025 to $18.3 billion in 2030, and the number of users will surpass 50 million.
BCG’s report estimates that mobile in-app purchases in 2025 will approach $130 billion, nearly half of global industry revenue.

records.evidence:
Additional highlights from the AI and Cloud-native Security April 2026 Advanced Research Report: The broader enterprise AI systems spend base, anchoring the forecast, is expected to reach nearly $400B by 2030, underscoring that the AISS opportunity is tied to production AI adoption rather than public cloud spending alone.

sourceContent.headline: Edge AI in Smart Devices Market
sourceContent.description: By 2035, the Edge AI in Smart Devices Market is projected to reach USD 179.2 Bn, up from USD 16.2 Bn in 2025, at a CAGR of 27.2%
paragraphs: In addition, OICA reported that global vehicle production reached 96.4 million units in 2025, with Asia Pacific accounting for more than 60% of global output, strengthening demand for edge AI applications in vehicles, including advanced driver assistance systems, cameras, sensors, and in-cabin intelligence.

According to IDC, around 370 million GenAI smartphones are expected to be shipped in 2025, representing nearly 30% of total smartphone shipments and highlighting the rapid transition toward AI-enabled handsets.
Last updated on July 20, 2026 Edge AI in smart IoT devices can reduce end-to-end latency by up to 45% compared with cloud-centric processing, because more decisions are made directly on the device.

Home ➤ Semiconductor and Electronics ➤ Edge AI in Smart Devices Market Revenue 2025 (US$B) 16.2 Bn Forecast 2035 (US$B) 179.2 Bn CAGR 2026-2035 27.2% Leading Region Asia Pacific This report has been updated 2 times .

Optimized edge-AI models running on smart sensors and cameras can deliver a combined gain of about 45% latency reduction and around 8–10 percentage-point higher inference accuracy versus unoptimized cloud-only models for similar tasks.

Smartphone battery platforms engineered for intensive on-device AI workloads can reach energy densities above 900 Wh/L , capacities around 7,350 mAh (approximately 26.3 Wh ), fast-charge to 20% in 5 minutes and 50% in 15 minutes , and sustain over 900 charge–discharge cycles under typical usage.
In 2025, the Global Edge AI in Smart Devices Market was valued at USD 16.2 billion and is projected to reach approximately USD 179.2 billion by 2035, growing at a 27.2% CAGR.
Asia Pacific dominated the Edge AI in Smart Devices Market in 2025, capturing a 38.0% share with approximately USD 6.14 billion in revenue.

According to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), nearly 6 billion people were using the internet in 2025, representing about 74% of the global population, with more than 240 million users added within a year.

GSMA Intelligence forecasts approximately 38.7 billion IoT connections by 2030, highlighting the need for edge AI solutions capable of processing data from billions of sensors, machines, and connected devices.
ITU data indicates that internet penetration across Asia Pacific reached around 77% of the population, creating a large and expanding user base for AI-enabled devices and connected services.

Combined with global smartphone shipments exceeding 1.24 billion units in 2024 and continued 5G expansion, the region’s concentration of device manufacturing and connected consumers positions Asia Pacific as the primary growth engine for edge AI adoption across smartphones, automotive systems, industrial IoT , and smart infrastructure through 2035.
Smartphones led the device type segment with a 38.00% share, supported by growing integration of AI-powered cameras, assistants, and on-device intelligence.
Computer Vision was the leading AI capability segment with a 30.00% share, fueled by demand for facial recognition , intelligent imaging, and AR/VR applications.
Consumer Electronics dominated the end-user segment with a 50.00% share, supported by rising adoption of AI-enabled smartphones, wearables, and smart home devices.
Asia Pacific was the dominant regional market with a 38.00% share, driven by strong electronics manufacturing, connected device adoption, and automotive technology growth.

Processors and Chips dominated the component segment of the Edge AI in Smart Devices Market, accounting for approximately 45% of component revenues, reflecting the structural dominance of hardware in enabling on-device intelligence.

Authoritative industry and technical sources indicate that edge AI hardware, particularly AI accelerator chips such as GPUs, FPGAs , ASICs , and NPUs, captures the largest share of value, with accelerator devices alone contributing around 40–44% of edge AI hardware revenues in recent base years.

Software and Frameworks represent the fastest-growing component segment in the Edge AI in Smart Devices Market, with dedicated edge AI software markets expanding at annual growth rates of approximately 29–35% , exceeding overall edge AI market growth.

Smartphones dominated the Edge AI in Smart Devices Market by device type, accounting for an estimated 40–42% of the global mobile AI application market, driven by their massive installed base, high shipment volumes, and rapid integration of on-device AI capabilities.
In 2025, global smartphone shipments reached approximately 1.24–1.26 billion units , creating the largest deployment platform for edge AI inference across consumer devices.

Computer Vision dominated the AI capability segment in the Edge AI in Smart Devices Market, accounting for approximately 30% of Edge AI capabilities, driven by widespread adoption across smartphones, IoT devices, security systems, and industrial applications.

Global smartphone shipments reached around 1.25 billion units in 2025, creating a massive installed base of camera-enabled devices where computer vision workloads such as image enhancement, facial authentication, and augmented reality are increasingly processed directly on-device.

Connected IoT devices are projected to reach approximately 21.1 billion by 2025, with many integrating cameras and visual sensors for applications including smart security, industrial inspection, and autonomous navigation.

In addition, OICA reported that global vehicle production reached 96.4 million units in 2025, with Asia Pacific accounting for more than 60% of global output, strengthening demand for edge AI applications in vehicles, including advanced driver assistance systems, cameras, sensors, and in-cabin intelligence. According to IDC, around 370 million GenAI smartphones are expected to be shipped in 2025, representing nearly 30% of total smartphone shipments and highlighting the rapid transition toward AI-enabled handsets. Last updated on July 20, 2026 Edge AI in smart IoT devices can reduce end-to-end latency by up to 45% compared with cloud-centric processing, because more decisions are made directly on the device.

68% prioritise AI features in next smartphone, but 82% say trust will decide the purchase: Report AI has overtaken design, price and battery life in purchase priorities, while consumers increasingly demand transparent data practices and on-device AI processing.

A new study by CyberMedia Research (CMR) found that 68% of consumers now prioritise AI capabilities when evaluating smartphones, while 82% said transparent data practices are essential for trusting AI-powered experiences.
The study found that 61% of respondents believe on-device AI processing improves both responsiveness and privacy, indicating growing awareness of how AI functions on smartphones.
Performance remains the most important consideration for smartphone buyers, cited by 78% of respondents, followed by camera quality, including AI enhancements (70%), and AI features (59%).

When choosing between similarly priced devices, 60% of consumers said they prefer a smartphone that offers both strong AI capabilities and powerful hardware, while 25% described themselves as AI-first buyers.
The trend is particularly strong among younger consumers, with 72% of Gen Z respondents saying AI will influence their next smartphone purchase, compared with 65% of millennials.

AI-powered photography continues to be the most widely used application, with 77% of respondents regularly using features such as low-light enhancement, portrait optimisation and intelligent scene detection.
While 66% of female consumers primarily use AI for camera and imaging features, 42% of male respondents prioritise productivity and communication use cases.
CMR also referenced its India Mobile Handset Market Review Report, which found that MediaTek accounted for 47% of smartphone chipset shipments in India.
The survey additionally reported that 93% of MediaTek users expressed satisfaction with their devices, while more than 45% said they would prefer a MediaTek-powered smartphone.

Also read: Influencer-driven sales in India rise 28% in first half of 2026: Report "Consumers increasingly evaluate AI experiences through the lens of trust, privacy and real-world utility. This shift is likely to influence how AI is designed, communicated and differentiated across future smartphone generations," said Sourabh Pandey, Analyst at CyberMedia Research. However, as AI adoption accelerates, buyers are also demanding greater transparency over how their data is used, with trust emerging as a key differentiator for smartphone brands.

sourceContent.headline: Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning
sourceContent.description: Dentsu Digital's first with AI Lab survey found about one in three private AI users consult AI before purchases, with travel and finance leading.
paragraphs: Valid responses totaled 10,000 for the screening survey and 3,300 for the main survey.
Its first survey, titled "Consumer AI Usage Survey 2026.7," examined how AI is being used in purchasing behavior and decision-making.
Dentsu Digital said the findings show AI use is spreading in awareness, comparison and post-purchase phases, while people still account for a higher share of decision-making at the final stage.
Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning

Dentsu Digital launches with AI Lab and publishes a July 2026 survey on consumer AI use in purchasing About one in three private AI users consult AI before purchases, with travel and financial categories above 50% AI use is strongest in awareness, comparison and post-purchase stages, while final buying decisions remain more human-led Dentsu Digital said on July 23 that about one in three consumers who use artificial intelligence in their private lives had consulted AI about purchases made within the past six months, releasing the first findings from a new in-house research unit focused on consumer behavior in the AI era.

The ratio was highest in higher-involvement categories where consumers tend to compare options more closely, with 57% in travel planning and accommodation bookings and 56% in financial products and insurance.

Across product categories, 2% to 3% of respondents said they adopted AI responses as-is for their final decision, indicating that some consumers are beginning to leave the ultimate purchase choice to AI.

Released on July 10, 2026, for ¥33K (~$203), the report is JOGA's 22nd annual industry survey.
Famitsu also reported that 73% of surveyed online game companies had implemented out-of-app payments, while 20% were considering doing so.

Other industry surveys have put adoption closer to 40% to 50%.

sourceContent.description: Survey of 400 marketers in four markets shows 88% producing more content while quality stalls. Which inputs brands feed generative tools now decides advantage.
paragraphs: A MiQ survey from November 2025, reported by PPC Land , found 72% of marketers planning AI adoption growth while only 45% felt confident.
by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

A Taboola study across a publisher network of roughly 600 million daily active users found AI-generated creatives increased or maintained click-through rates without damaging conversion rates , with strongest results in food and drink and personal finance and more muted outcomes in categories such as education.
Only 45% of marketers gain quality from AI, WARC and TikTok find

According to the survey, 90% of marketers agree generative AI has become a key tool in the creative development process, 72% use it frequently as a regular part of content production, and 87% believe their organisation is using it effectively for creative development.
WARC's Marketer's Toolkit found that 59% of marketers agree traditional demographic segmentation is no longer effective.
Yet the new survey found demographic data remains the primary input used to brief AI, relied on by 67% of respondents.
Only 17% of marketers make it a rule to always incorporate community or audience insights beyond demographics into generative AI workflows.

Asked to identify the biggest gaps in inputs currently available when briefing generative AI, respondents pointed first to audience behavioural data covering how people engage rather than who they are, cited by 45%.
Access to real-time cultural or community signals and tools that translate insights into effective AI briefs each registered 35%.
Only 10% of respondents said they do not perceive significant gaps in the inputs available to them.

According to the survey, 86% of marketers agree audience behaviour and community signals will influence creative development significantly more over the next three years, and one in three believe access to richer audience or cultural signals would do most to unlock generative AI advantage.
The WARC and TikTok figure of 87% of marketers believing their organisation uses generative AI effectively sits awkwardly against other industry measurement.
The same MIQ Global AI Confidence Curve is cited inside the WARC report itself for a separate finding: only 40% of marketers strongly believe they can apply findings from one campaign to another.
A self-reported 87% effectiveness rating from a vendor-commissioned survey and a 45% confidence rating from an independent one describe the same industry.
Brandwatch survey findings reported in April 2026 identified social listening and consumer research as a top skill gap at 55%, with cross-platform content optimisation at 52%.

sourceContent.headline: Foldable smartphones are moving into a pivotal 2026
sourceContent.description: Omdia reports foldable smartphone shipments are flat in 2025 but forecasts a 50% rebound in 2026. Read our analysis of market hurdles and strategic value.
paragraphs: The second-largest foldable market, the US, grew modestly by 7% in H1 2025, driven mainly by Motorola’s Razr 2025 series.

They are a proving ground for whether hardware R&D can still deliver meaningful differentiation in an industry where the gravitational pull is shifting toward software, artificial intelligence, and services as the core revenue drivers.
Consequently, the scale and wider strategic relevance of foldable smartphones is moving up the priority list.
Even though the category is more crowded, global shipments were flat at 6.6 million units in H1 2025.
China was the major exception, growing 32.8% year-on-year, predominantly driven by Huawei’s Mate and Pura X models.
Even though vendors are experiencing above-expected momentum with their recent launches, global foldable shipments are forecast to remain flat at 17.2 million units for the full year.
Omdia forecasts foldable smartphone shipments to grow by a staggering 50% YoY in 2026 and carry momentum into 2027.
Foldables remain a niche in shipment terms, making up between 1.0-1.5% of global volumes and only 5% of devices priced above US$700.
One Galaxy Z Fold7 sold at list price (around US$1899) generates the equivalent revenue of roughly 15 entry-level Galaxy A06 4Gs.
In 2024, only 15% of Samsung’s smartphones sold worldwide were priced above US$1,000 (Galaxy S and Z).
However, these devices contributed a staggering 44% of shipment value.
Within that tier, foldables (Galaxy Z and W) contributed more than 20% of volume, helping lift ASPs and shift Samsung’s revenue mix away from the low-margin, hyper- competitive mass market.

In a recent consumer study conducted by Omdia across five global markets (N=5000) that focused on cutting-edge smartphone tech, 96% of respondents showed some level of familiarity with foldable smartphones.

However, almost 40% of respondents said they were not interested in foldable smartphones, and over a third of respondents stated they were interested but foldables sit outside their budget or don’t meet their needs.

Consequently, the scale and wider strategic relevance of foldable smartphones is moving up the priority list.

records.scope: 글로벌 스마트폰 위성 D2D 서비스 · 서비스 매출 기준
records.evidence:
Omdia estimates that cellular standard devices, meaning smartphones using 4G or 5G technologies to connect directly to satellites, will become the dominant model in the smartphone satellite D2D market, accounting for over 95% of global total MAUs by 2030.
This represents mean annual growth rates of 80.1% for users and 49.4% for revenue from 2026 to 2030.
“In contrast to dual-mode phone solutions, which require a proprietary satellite communication link in the smartphone, cellular standard based solutions, such as Starlink D2C and AST SpaceMobile, can directly connect to devices compliant with 4G or 5G standards, particularly existing smartphones,” noted Guang Yang, Senior Principal Analyst, Service Provider Strategies and Mobile Infrastructure, at Omdia .

records.evidence:
What is driving Qualcomm Inc (QCOM)’s stock price down today?
Reports suggesting accelerated timelines for major handset manufacturers to transition toward in-house connectivity solutions are creating headwinds for the company's long-term licensing and chip supply revenue.
Valuation and Margin Pressure: Following the recent stock price surge driven by AI optimism, the company faces "priced-for-perfection" risk, where any delay in the adoption of AI-enabled handsets or margin compression in the diversifying Automotive and IoT segments could trigger a sharp technical correction.

records.title: 71% young Indians use AI for career advice

values.label: 응답자 수
values.sourceLine: The report, titled 'The AI Companion Report: How Young Indians Are Learning, Working, and Making Decisions with AI', surveyed more than 2,000 respondents across India, most of them aged between 18 and 34 years.

values.label: 조사 인원
values.sourceLine: At PulseAI Research, we're building AI that transforms billions of consumer signals into validated, decision-ready intelligence, enabling brands to act with greater confidence instead of navigating a maze of disconnected predictive models.” PulseAI Research said the study was conducted among 2,000 consumers across India, with 88.2% of respondents belonging to the 18-34 age group, to understand changing perceptions, usage patterns and trust in AI.

values.label: 기간
values.sourceLine: The report, titled 'The AI Companion Report: How Young Indians Are Learning, Working, and Making Decisions with AI', surveyed more than 2,000 respondents across India, most of them aged between 18 and 34 years.

values.label: 응답 비중
values.sourceLine: According to the study, 70.6% of respondents have already used AI for career advice, while 62% said they would be comfortable using it for career coaching in the future.

values.label: 응답 비중
values.sourceLine: The report found that 41.4% of respondents now turn to AI before using search engines when looking for information online.

values.label: 응답 비중
values.sourceLine: Learning emerged as the biggest use case for AI, with 29.8% of respondents saying they primarily use it for studying and learning, followed by research and information gathering (22.3%).

The next frontier is deterministic future intelligence, AI that continuously learns from real consumer behaviour, validates every signal, and enables businesses to act with far greater confidence about what comes next.

New Delhi: A majority of young Indians are using artificial intelligence (AI) beyond work and productivity, with over 70% seeking career advice from AI tools and nearly half saying their daily lives would be disrupted if they lost access to AI for a week, according to a study by PulseAI Research, the consumer insights division of Smytten.
According to the study, 70.6% of respondents have already used AI for career advice, while 62% said they would be comfortable using it for career coaching in the future.
The report found that 41.4% of respondents now turn to AI before using search engines when looking for information online.
Learning emerged as the biggest use case for AI, with 29.8% of respondents saying they primarily use it for studying and learning, followed by research and information gathering (22.3%).

At PulseAI Research, we're building AI that transforms billions of consumer signals into validated, decision-ready intelligence, enabling brands to act with greater confidence instead of navigating a maze of disconnected predictive models.” PulseAI Research said the study was conducted among 2,000 consumers across India, with 88.2% of respondents belonging to the 18-34 age group, to understand changing perceptions, usage patterns and trust in AI.

localization.title: 71%의 젊은 인도인이 진로 조언을 위해 AI를 사용함
summaryLines: 'AI 동행 보고서 · 젊은 인도인들이 AI를 통해 학습하고, 일하고, 의사결정하는 방법'이라는 제목의 이 보고서는 인도 전역의 2,000명 이상의 응답자를 대상으로 설문조사를 실시했으며, 이들 중 대부분은 18세에서 34세 사이였음
다음 개척지는 실제 소비자 행동으로부터 지속적으로 학습하고, 모든 신호를 검증하며, 기업이 다음에 일어날 일에 대해 훨씬 더 큰 확신을 갖고 행동할 수 있도록 지원하는 결정론적 미래 인텔리전스인 AI임
뉴델리 · Smytten의 소비자 통찰력 부문인 PulseAI Research의 연구에 따르면 대다수의 젊은 인도인은 업무와 생산성을 넘어서 인공 지능(AI)을 사용하고 있으며, 70% 이상이 AI 도구에서 직업 조언을 구하고 거의 절반이 일주일 동안 AI에 대한 액세스를 잃으면 일상 생활이 중단될 것이라고 말함

records.evidence:
China approved Apple Intelligence following early numbers showing Apple’s mainland shipments up 24.4% in Q2, as the overall market slipped 4.3%.
Early IDC numbers point to a stark divide between Apple and the rest of the market: Applying Apple’s share to IDC’s 66 million-unit estimate, Apple moved about 11.9 million phones, up from 9.6 million in the same period last year.
China’s cyberspace regulator said Apple Intelligence was one of seven phone-based generative AI services to finish registration, which is needed before they can launch to the public.

Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) cleared for China AI launch as iPhone sales test 24% jump
Apple hit a new high of $325.65, then traded at $324.03.
That puts Apple’s market cap at $4.77 trillion, 39.2 times its trailing earnings.
IDC’s estimates, rounded, show Apple shipped about 2.4 million more iPhones year-on-year in mainland China in the June quarter.
Apple was up 2.9% to $324.03 late in the morning, hitting a new intraday high and tacking on roughly $135 billion in market cap.
Net sales in the region climbed 28% to $20.5 billion in the March quarter, making up 18.4% of its total revenue.
KeyBanc Capital Markets’ Brandon Nispel downgraded Apple to Underweight, set a $250 target, and pointed to slower device upgrades.
He sees Services growing 7% in fiscal 2027, well below the nearly 12% the market is pricing in.
But Morgan Stanley NYSE:MS analyst Erik Woodring stuck with his Overweight call and $360 target, saying product price hikes could add 2% to 4% to fiscal Q3 EPS and about 1% to fiscal 2027 EPS.
IDC is warning China’s market drop might hit 20% in the second half if things stay as they are.

sourceContent.headline: Intel Q2 2026 Revenue Surges 25% as AI Server Chips, Foundry Business and PC Demand Fuel Strongest Growth in 15 Years - InfotechLead
sourceContent.description: Intel delivered its strongest quarterly revenue growth during the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure
paragraphs: Intel reported Q2 2026 revenue of $16.1 billion, an increase of 25 percent, significantly above its guidance range of $14.4 billion to $15.4 billion.
Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) delivered $6.3 billion in revenue with 13 percent increase as demand shifted toward premium AI-enabled PCs.

Intel delivered its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than 15 years during the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure, data center processors, premium PC chips and expanding foundry services.
Intel Q2 2026 Revenue Surges 25% as AI Server Chips, Foundry Business and PC Demand Fuel Strongest Growth in 15 Years - InfotechLead
Revenue surged 59 percent to $6.3 billion, supported by adoption of Xeon 6 processors, increasing AI server deployments and rising demand for CPUs powering agentic AI workloads.
Omdia said more than half of B2B channel partners reported customers postponing hardware refresh plans until market conditions stabilize, while 6 percent expect outright cancellations.
Intel Foundry generated $5.8 billion in revenue, representing 31 percent growth.

Reflecting confidence in future demand, Intel increased its planned 2026 capital expenditure to $20 billion, up from earlier expectations, to expand manufacturing capacity and meet rising AI-driven processor demand.

Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses

New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.
The report estimates that the disability consumer market is now worth $675 billion, equivalent in size to the global beauty and cosmetics industry.
Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.
Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.
Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.

“The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”
The study found that: Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.
Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

“If the momentum achieved over the past 10 years is any indication of what the future holds, then we can project with confidence that the favourable trends identified in our research will bear brighter tomorrows for the disability community, businesses at large and the US economy overall.”

summaryLines: Disability:IN과 AIR(American Institutes for Research)의 새로운 주요 연구에 따르면 미국 장애 소비자 시장은 약 6,750억 달러 규모로 성장했으며, 이는 접근성, 포용적 제품 및 장애 중심 고객 전략에 투자하는 기업에 상당한 상업적 기회가 있음을 강조함
보고서, 차세대 성장 시장 · 6,750억 달러 규모의 소비자 기회 내부에서는 근로 연령 성인 장애인(16~64세)의 구매력을 조사하고 모든 부문의 기업이 장애인 소비자의 요구 사항을 더 잘 충족하는 제품, 서비스 및 고객 경험을 설계함으로써 이익을 얻을 수 있다고 주장함
이전에 보고된 바와 같이, 연구에 따르면 전 세계 장애 시장의 연간 소비 규모는 미화 13조 달러에 달해 세계 최대의 소비자 부문 중 하나임

summaryLines: 2026년 7월 17일 08:48(ET) | 출처 · BCC Research LLC BCC Research LLC 보스턴, 2026년 7월 17일(GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- 글로벌 가축 모니터링 시장(Global Livestock Monitoring Market)이라는 제목의 BCC Research의 새 보고서에 따르면 전 세계 가축 모니터링 시장은 2025년 62억 달러에서 2030년까지 103억 달러로 연평균 복합 성장률(CAGR) 10.6%로 성장할 것으로 예상됨

소비자 제품 및 서비스 뉴스 자동차 및 부품 뉴스 산업 및 유틸리티 뉴스 항공우주 및 방위 뉴스 “BCC Research에 따르면 전 세계 가축 모니터링 시장은 AI 지원 정밀 농업, IoT 센서, 웨어러블 기술의 채택 증가와 동물 건강, 생산성 및 추적성에 대한 수요 증가에 힘입어 2024년 56억 달러에서 2030년까지 103억 달러로 CAGR 10.6%로 성장할 것으로 예상됨”
• 강력한 시장 확장 · 가축 모니터링 시장은 축산업의 디지털화 가속화와 유제품, 쇠고기 및 가금류 운영 전반에 걸쳐 데이터 기반 가축 관리에 대한 필요성 증가로 인해 2030년까지 CAGR 10.6%의 강력한 두 자릿수 성장을 경험할 것임

sourceContent.headline: 85% of Indian CFOs Face Pressure to Prove AI ROI: Avalara Study
sourceContent.description: Indian finance leaders are accelerating AI adoption, but governance is falling behind. Avalara finds 85% face ROI pressure, while accountability and audit readiness remain gaps.
paragraphs: The report suggests governance frameworks have yet to catch up with the pace of AI adoption. 27% of Indian respondents said accountability for significant AI agent errors is either unclear or assigned to no one, the highest share among respondents in India, the US, the UK, and Australia. 24% have not updated internal controls in the past year to reflect AI-driven decisions.
An Avalara study finds Indian finance leaders are accelerating AI adoption, but governance is lagging, leaving accountability, audit readiness, and compliance gaps unresolved.

According to Avalara's report, Agents of Change: How the Race to Deploy AI Agents Is Outrunning Financial Governance, 85% of Indian finance leaders say they face moderate or significant career pressure to prove that AI agent investments are generating returns.
The survey also found that 71% believe the focus inside their organizations is on deploying AI agents quickly, while only 8% say governance takes priority over speed.

Only 28% say AI controls have been reviewed by IT or cybersecurity teams. 10% are not confident they could clearly explain an AI agent's decisions to regulators or auditors, a higher share than respondents in the US, the UK, and Australia.
The survey also found that 76% of Indian finance leaders lack dedicated in-house expertise to fully understand how their AI agents work.

According to IDC's Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker, spending reached $89.7 billion in Q1 2026, up 33% year-over-year but flat sequentially as growth normalizes off a larger base.
IDC raised its full-year 2026 forecast to $497 billion on hyperscaler capex growth and emerging non-GPU AI demand.
IDC now projects the global AI infrastructure market will surpass $1 trillion in 2029, reaching $1.08 trillion, before climbing to $1.21 trillion in 2030.
The United States remained dominant at $67.9 billion (75.7% of global spend, +30.3% YoY), though growth continues to moderate.
China (PRC) returned to growth at $7.8 billion (8.7% share, +9.3% YoY).
The Middle East & Africa remained the fastest-growing region (+233% YoY to $1.1 billion), followed by APeJC (+62% to $5.8 billion) and Western Europe (up to $5.1 billion).
Server spending represented 97.6% of total AI infrastructure value in Q1 2026, and within that, a growing share of AI-centric demand is landing on infrastructure that isn’t GPU-accelerated at all.

Pent-up storage refresh is now landing on top of genuine AI-driven demand, reinforcing the urgency behind external storage strategy even as AI-centric storage remains a small share (2.4%) of total AI infrastructure value.

We watched x86 accelerated servers fall from $52 billion to $35 billion in just two quarters while ARM rack-scale platforms nearly doubled, and that’s not demand destruction, that’s an architecture shift that is yet to be definitive as new x86 platforms are on the horizon as well.
Q1 2026’s 33% year-over-year growth reflects a much higher base, not a slowdown in demand.

Yes, Non-x86 (ARM) accelerated server value climbed to $53.0 billion in Q1 2026, up from $47.5 billion in Q4 2025 and $29.8 billion in Q3 2025, while x86 accelerated value fell to $34.6 billion from $42.7 billion and $51.9 billion over the same span.

paragraphs: Global spending on AI infrastructure reached $89.7 billion in the first quarter of 2026, representing a 33.1 percent increase year on year, according to IDC’s Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker.

IDC reported that non-x86 (ARM) accelerated servers generated $53.0 billion in spending during the quarter, compared with $34.6 billion for x86 systems, highlighting a significant shift in AI data center deployments, Juan Seminara, Research Director, Worldwide Infrastructure Trackers, IDC, said in a blog post .

While spending on AI infrastructure remained flat compared with the previous quarter as growth normalized from a higher base, AI infrastructure market has entered a new phase driven by long-term investment commitments, architecture shifts, and expanding enterprise AI deployments.
IDC: Global AI Infrastructure Spending Hits $89.7 Billion in Q1 2026, ARM Servers Overtake x86 as Market Heads Toward $1.21 Trillion by 2030 - InfotechLead

IDC has raised its full-year 2026 AI infrastructure spending forecast to $497 billion, reflecting continued hyperscaler capital expenditure, growing enterprise adoption, and rising demand for AI infrastructure beyond GPU-based computing.
The global AI infrastructure market will exceed $1.08 trillion in 2029 before reaching $1.21 trillion in 2030, representing a five-year CAGR of approximately 30 percent from 2025.
Server infrastructure dominated AI spending, accounting for $87.6 billion, or 97.6 percent of total AI infrastructure investment.
Storage spending reached $2.2 billion, representing 2.4 percent of the market.

United States Maintains Leadership While Middle East Records Fastest Growth The United States remained the world’s largest AI infrastructure market with $67.9 billion in spending during Q1 2026, representing 75.7 percent of global investment and growing 30.3 percent year over year.
China returned to growth with $7.8 billion, accounting for 8.7 percent of worldwide spending and expanding 9.3 percent compared with a year earlier.

The Middle East and Africa emerged as the fastest-growing region globally, with spending increasing 233 percent year over year to $1.1 billion, supported by sovereign AI initiatives and government-backed investments.

Asia Pacific excluding Japan and China (APeJC) region recorded 62 percent growth to $5.8 billion, while Western Europe reached $5.1 billion as governments and enterprises accelerated AI infrastructure deployment.

AI Infrastructure Spending Continues Multi-Year Expansion Global AI infrastructure spending reached $318 billion in 2025, more than doubling from $153 billion in 2024, which itself represented 107.6 percent year-over-year growth.
AI infrastructure spending will expand by approximately 56 percent in 2026, an upward revision from its previous estimate of around 53 percent growth.

summaryLines: IDC의 Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker에 따르면 AI 인프라에 대한 전 세계 지출은 2026년 1분기에 897억 달러에 달해 전년 동기 대비 33.1% 증가함
IDC는 비 x86(ARM) 가속 서버가 해당 분기 동안 530억 달러의 지출을 창출했다고 보고했으며 x86 시스템의 경우 346억 달러에 비해 이는 AI 데이터 센터 배포의 중요한 변화를 강조했다고 IDC의 Worldwide Infrastructure Trackers 연구 이사인 Juan Seminara가 블로그 게시물에서 말함
성장이 더 높은 기반에서 정상화됨에 따라 AI 인프라에 대한 지출은 이전 분기에 비해 변동이 없었지만, AI 인프라 시장은 장기 투자 약속, 아키텍처 전환 및 엔터프라이즈 AI 배포 확대에 힘입어 새로운 단계에 진입함

paragraphs: Worldwide end-user spending on AI models and platforms is projected to total US$64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from US$39 billion in 2025, with more and more enterprises are choosing to work with companies that can provide clear value.
This dynamic is accelerating growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised models, which are forecast to grow 210 percent in 2026.

Gartner predicts AI models and platforms spend to hit US$64B - ARN

Spending on generative AI (genAI) models is forecast to grow 117 per cent while AI platform spending will rise 36.9 per cent in 2026, according to Gartner’s latest forecast on AI platforms and models. “Enterprise AI budgets are coming under greater scrutiny, with increased focus on usage efficiency, cost control and measurable outcomes ,” said the analyst firm’s senior principal research analyst, Arunasree Cheparthi. “Spending is shifting toward providers who can demonstrate clear value across cost, latency, performance, and reliability. “This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency, and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use.” However, as spending becomes more usage-driven, providers face pressure to demonstrate real adoption, sustained use, and durable margins.

According to Gartner, the AI software market is forecast to grow significantly between 2025 and 2026, with total market revenue increasing from US$39.3 billion to US$64.3 billion, representing 63.4 per cent growth.
Meanwhile, the fastest-growing segment is DSLMs and specialised genAI models, which is projected to expand from US$1.6 billion to US$4.9 billion, achieving 210.0 per cent growth.

AI application development platforms are forecast to grow from US$6.9 billion to US$9.5 billion (up 38.6 per cent), and AI platforms for data science and machine learning are expected to increase from US$19.4 billion to US$26.4 billion (an increase of 36.3 per cent).

Overall, these projections highlight accelerating investment in generative AI technologies, particularly in specialised AI and foundation models . “Over the long-term, the biggest winners will be vendors that help enterprises manage where and how AI is used across the business ,” said Cheparthi. “As more models enter the market and usage-based pricing becomes harder to predict, buyers will turn to platforms that help them choose the right tools, monitor performance , enforce policy and keep costs under control.” Equinix passes top Australian leadership to Jarrod Nink Cohesity promotes Peter Hanna to lead growth in Asia Pacific and Japan As White House monitors latest OpenAI incident, Congress eyes an AI ‘kill switch’ for DHS news EDGE 2026: Becoming the successful MSP for the future 28 Jul 2026 6 mins news EDGE 2026: The MSP of the future 27 Jul 2026 4 mins news AI data centre growth ignites debate over power, water, and infrastructure 27 Jul 2026 11 mins news Monvia lists on ASX after $17.5M IPO 24 Jul 2026 2 mins news SoftwareOne adds NinjaOne to portfolio 24 Jul 2026 2 mins news Adactin teams up with Cyara to support AI-powered customer service 23 Jul 2026 2 mins news Synnex strengthens Microsoft practice with four Microsoft specialisations 23 Jul 2026 3 mins news Datacom considers next steps for local MD role as Laura Malcolm departs 22 Jul 2026 3 mins Leading Edge DC hires Schneider Electric’s Joe Craparotta as CEO Ingram Micro Australia added to Oracle’s Cloud Distribution Program

sourceContent.headline: AI Coding Tools Hit $9B as Pricing Goes Metered
sourceContent.description: GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Claude Code are ditching flat fees for pay-per-token billing in 2026. Here is what's driving the AI pricing shift.
paragraphs: Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.

Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.
AI Coding Tools Hit $9B as Pricing Goes Metered
Mordor Intelligence sizes the global AI code tools market at roughly $9.35 billion in 2026, expanding at more than 26% a year.
Copilot Pro still lists at $10 a month and Copilot Enterprise at $39 per user per month, but both now sit on top of a metered layer that tracks actual usage rather than assuming it away.

GitHub’s own research previously found that Copilot users complete tasks about 55% faster than developers coding without it, a strong pitch for adoption but a rough one for margins once millions of developers start running agentic workflows against the same infrastructure.
A flat $20 monthly subscription only works if the average user’s token consumption stays well below what that fee actually covers.
That behaviour is a major reason Claude Code was reported to author close to 4% of all public GitHub commits by early 2026, a figure some analysts expect to pass 20% before the year is out.
The spread between roughly $9 billion and $34 billion for the same year comes down to scope.

Taking the narrower, more comparable estimates from Mordor Intelligence, Grand View Research, and Research and Markets, the market sits close to $9 to $10 billion in 2026 and is on track for somewhere between $19 billion and $26 billion by 2030.

Surveys circulating in early 2026 put Claude Code’s “most loved” rating among senior engineers at 46%, against 19% for Cursor and 9% for GitHub Copilot, and separate JetBrains-linked data credits Claude Code with a 91% customer satisfaction score and a net promoter score of 54, the highest reported in the category.

In startups under 50 employees, Claude Code adoption reportedly reaches 75% against 42% for Cursor, while GitHub Copilot holds a commanding 56% share inside companies with more than 10,000 employees, largely on the back of existing Microsoft procurement relationships.
Copilot’s installed base remains enormous regardless, with more than 15 million developers across upwards of 77,000 organisations, including a reported 77% of the Fortune 500.

summaryLinesEn: Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.

Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.

sourceContent.headline: TSMC Q2 2026 Profit Soars 77% to Record T$706.6 bn as AI Chip Demand Drives Growth and Capex Rises - TelecomLead
sourceContent.description: TSMC, the world’s largest contract chipmaker and a key supplier to Nvidia and Apple, delivered a record-breaking second quarter in 2026
paragraphs: TSMC reported 77 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to a record T$706.6 billion (approximately $22 billion), significantly exceeding market expectations.

The 2nm process contributed 3 percent, 3nm accounted for 30 percent, and technologies 7nm and below represented 77 percent of total wafer revenue, highlighting the industry’s rapid transition toward leading-edge nodes for AI and high-performance computing workloads.

The strong financial performance was driven by sustained demand for advanced semiconductor technologies, including 3nm and 2nm process nodes and advanced CoWoS chip packaging, which are critical for AI accelerators and high-performance computing applications.
TSMC Q2 2026 Profit Soars 77% to Record T$706.6 bn as AI Chip Demand Drives Growth and Capex Rises - TelecomLead

High Performance Computing (HPC) remained TSMC’s largest business segment, contributing 66 percent of total revenue as demand for AI GPUs, AI accelerators and custom processors from major customers such as Nvidia, AMD, Apple and Broadcom continued to surge.
TSMC’s smartphone business accounted for 22 percent of revenue despite seasonal softness.
TSMC’s Internet of Things (IoT) segment contributed 6 percent.
Automotive represented 3 percent of revenue, Digital Consumer Electronics (DCE) generated 1 percent, and other businesses contributed the remaining 2 percent.
The latest Omdia report said global smartphone shipments dropped 4 percent in 2Q26 as the memory crisis disrupted supply and pushed up component costs.
Apple, one of the main customers of TSMC, has increased its smartphone market share to 20 percent in Q2 2026 from 16 percent in Q2 2025.
Geographically, North America generated 78 percent of TSMC’s revenue in the second quarter, underlining the company’s growing dependence on U.S. hyperscale cloud providers and AI chip designers.
Asia Pacific accounted for 8 percent, China contributed 6 percent, while Japan and Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) each represented 4 percent of total revenue.
TSMC also maintained a positive outlook, forecasting more than 40 percent revenue growth for full-year 2026, supported by robust AI infrastructure investments from global technology companies.
Reflecting confidence in long-term AI demand, TSMC increased its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to between $60 billion and $64 billion, up from its earlier upper-end estimate of $56 billion.
The company also announced an additional $100 billion investment in Arizona, expanding its total planned U.S. investment to $265 billion.

TSMC’s market capitalization has climbed to approximately $1.97 trillion, nearly double that of Samsung Electronics, underscoring its dominant position in the global semiconductor industry, Reuters news report said.

TSMC reported 77 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to a record T$706.6 billion (approximately $22 billion), significantly exceeding market expectations.

High Performance Computing (HPC) remained TSMC’s largest business segment, contributing 66 percent of total revenue as demand for AI GPUs, AI accelerators and custom processors from major customers such as Nvidia, AMD, Apple and Broadcom continued to surge.
TSMC’s smartphone business accounted for 22 percent of revenue despite seasonal softness.
TSMC’s Internet of Things (IoT) segment contributed 6 percent.
Automotive represented 3 percent of revenue, Digital Consumer Electronics (DCE) generated 1 percent, and other businesses contributed the remaining 2 percent.

The 2nm process contributed 3 percent, 3nm accounted for 30 percent, and technologies 7nm and below represented 77 percent of total wafer revenue, highlighting the industry’s rapid transition toward leading-edge nodes for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
The latest Omdia report said global smartphone shipments dropped 4 percent in 2Q26 as the memory crisis disrupted supply and pushed up component costs.
Apple, one of the main customers of TSMC, has increased its smartphone market share to 20 percent in Q2 2026 from 16 percent in Q2 2025.
Geographically, North America generated 78 percent of TSMC’s revenue in the second quarter, underlining the company’s growing dependence on U.S. hyperscale cloud providers and AI chip designers.
Asia Pacific accounted for 8 percent, China contributed 6 percent, while Japan and Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) each represented 4 percent of total revenue.
TSMC also maintained a positive outlook, forecasting more than 40 percent revenue growth for full-year 2026, supported by robust AI infrastructure investments from global technology companies.
Reflecting confidence in long-term AI demand, TSMC increased its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to between $60 billion and $64 billion, up from its earlier upper-end estimate of $56 billion.
The company also announced an additional $100 billion investment in Arizona, expanding its total planned U.S. investment to $265 billion.

records.evidence:
If 60 percent of the bill sits in refinement loops rather than primary inference, and most budget frameworks were built around inference costs alone, the gap between forecast and actual spend will widen as agentic deployments scale.
The findings from its May 2026 FinOps survey already suggest that the budget conversation has moved from the IT team to the C-suite, and it is unlikely to move back.
McKinsey's July 2026 report, published in the McKinsey Quarterly and authored by researchers from QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, pinpoints response refinement as the dominant cost driver: 60 percent of total agentic AI spend goes not to the first inference call but to the iterative cycles of checking, correcting, and improving that agents run before delivering a usable output.

sourceContent.headline: 60% of agentic AI costs go to response refinement, and most enterprises are already over budget
sourceContent.description: McKinsey's July 2026 report reveals 93% of enterprises exceed AI budgets, with 60% of agentic costs tied to response refinement, not raw compute.
paragraphs: If 60 percent of the bill sits in refinement loops rather than primary inference, and most budget frameworks were built around inference costs alone, the gap between forecast and actual spend will widen as agentic deployments scale.
The findings from its May 2026 FinOps survey already suggest that the budget conversation has moved from the IT team to the C-suite, and it is unlikely to move back.

McKinsey's July 2026 report, published in the McKinsey Quarterly and authored by researchers from QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, pinpoints response refinement as the dominant cost driver: 60 percent of total agentic AI spend goes not to the first inference call but to the iterative cycles of checking, correcting, and improving that agents run before delivering a usable output.
Inference on GPT-3.5-level capability cost $20 per million tokens in early 2024 and fell to $0.07 by year's end, according to the Stanford HAI 2025 AI Index cited in McKinsey's new report.

LLM expenditures tripled over a 12-month period by the end of 2025, according to a Menlo Ventures study also cited by McKinsey, and 93 percent of organizations surveyed by McKinsey in May 2026 reported exceeding their AI budgets.
McKinsey's Enterprise AI FinOps Survey, conducted in May 2026 with 75 qualified respondents across five major industries, found that 93 percent have already blown past their AI budgets.

sourceContent.headline: Google's $205 Billion AI Bet Terrified Investors. Here's Why the Market Was Wrong
sourceContent.description: Alphabet just posted its first negative free cash flow quarter as a public company, and Wall Street panicked. But the number investors fixated on may be the least important figure in the entire earnings report.
paragraphs: Alphabet's first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion masked Google Cloud's 82% revenue surge to $24.8 billion with operating margins tripling.

According to Alphabet’s earnings, Google is already converting AI investment into accelerating cloud revenue, expanding margins, and posting a record $514 billion backlog waiting to become future sales.
A record $514 billion signed cloud backlog means much of Alphabet's $205 billion capex is effectively pre-sold before the infrastructure even goes live.
Google's $205 Billion AI Bet Terrified Investors. Here's Why the Market Was Wrong
Free cash flow came in at negative $5.9 billion, a stunning reversal driven by an unprecedented surge in AI infrastructure spending.
Capital expenditures totaled $44.9 billion during the quarter, doubling from a year ago.
Even more surprising, management raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to $205 billion, signaling that spending is still accelerating rather than slowing.
Collectively, the industry’s largest AI builders are on pace to spend well over $700 billion in 2026.
Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% year over year to $24.8 billion.
Perhaps the most overlooked figure was Google’s $514 billion cloud backlog — signed customer contracts that haven’t yet been recognized as revenue.
Wall Street currently forecasts 23% revenue growth this year followed by 21% next year.
If Alphabet maintains roughly 20% annual growth into 2028, the company would exit that year generating approximately $2 billion in revenue every single day.

But if Alphabet continues executing at its current pace, today’s $205 billion investment program may eventually look less like reckless spending and more like the foundation of its next long-term competitive moat.

For the past 20 years he’s been cruising the markets looking for companies to lock up as long-term holdings in a portfolio while writing extensively on the broad sectors of consumer goods, technology, and industrials.

Matt Murphy: Inside the $500M Anthropic SPV That Changed Menlo Ventures — BigGo Finance
The deal was structurally awkward for Menlo Ventures, a firm that manages roughly $600 million per fund.
That $10 million starter check and the $500 million-plus SPV that followed would become the defining bet of his career.
The SPV itself was Menlo's first, raising over $500 million from limited partners and strategic investors in a process Murphy describes as the single hardest part of the entire deal.
"Never done before, over $500 million, first time," he said.

In applications where user experience directly drives business outcomes — where a 5% improvement in model quality translates to measurable gains in retention and revenue — companies will pay the premium.
Murphy frames it as an inevitable optimization for companies approaching $100 billion in revenue.
Lovable, an AI-first no-code app builder, rocketed from zero to $300 million in annual recurring revenue in roughly a year.
On one end: seed-stage "tracker checks" of $100,000 to $1 million into more than 50 companies per fund.
On the other end: concentrated, later-stage bets above $10 million in ARR, where a company has already emerged as a category leader.
Menlo's $3 billion in total fund commitments is calibrated to stay competitive: large enough to write lead checks, small enough to maintain cultural cohesion.

"You're better off being in them at a very small percent than owning a large percent of a company that exits for $300 to $500 million," Murphy said. paragraphs: Analytics provider Apptopia, first reported by Big Technology and later covered by Fortune , tracked ChatGPT’s app market share falling from 69.1% in January 2025 to 45.3% earlier in 2026, while Gemini’s app share rose from 14.7% to 25.2% across the same window.
The shift shows up just as clearly in Australia.
ChatGPT’s share of the market is shrinking while its user base and revenue keep climbing, because the overall AI-assistant market is expanding faster than ChatGPT alone can capture.
ChatGPT Market Share Falls to 46.4% [2026]

Sensor Tower’s State of AI 2026 report puts OpenAI’s chatbot at 46.4% of the global AI-assistant market at the end of May 2026, the first time it has held less than half the market since debuting in November 2022.
Google’s Gemini climbed to 27.7% over the same period, and Anthropic’s Claude reached 10.3%, according to the same tracking data reported by TechCrunch on June 16, 2026 .

ChatGPT’s Market Share Falls Below 50% for the First Time The Numbers Behind the Slide: Three Trackers, One Story Claude’s Enterprise Play: How Anthropic Is Cutting Into OpenAI’s Lead Australia’s AI Adoption Numbers: Telsyte’s June 2026 Snapshot Market Share vs Revenue: Why OpenAI Still Leads on Money Competitive Comparison: ChatGPT vs Gemini vs Claude at a Glance Historical Context: How Fast Tech Leaders Usually Lose Ground What This Means for Australian Businesses Choosing an AI Vendor Market Impact: Why Investors and Analysts Are Watching Closely Five Predictions: Where AI Assistant Market Share Goes Next Does ChatGPT’s falling market share mean it’s losing users?

Telsyte’s June 2026 research counts more than 17 million Australians using AI tools monthly, but ChatGPT’s local lead is narrowing too: 13.8 million users against Gemini’s 9.1 million and Claude’s 2.9 million, per Telsyte’s announcement .
By that measure, ChatGPT’s global AI-assistant market share slipped under the 50% mark in March 2026 and kept falling, landing at 46.4% by the end of May.
A year earlier, in December 2024, ChatGPT held 65.3% of the same market.

Google folded Gemini into Search, Android, and Workspace rather than asking users to go find and install a separate app, and that bundling shows up directly in the numbers: Gemini’s monthly active users reached 662 million by May 2026, up from a 6% market share in early 2025 to 27.7% by May.
Paid conversion sits at a modest 3.1%, far behind Claude’s rate, which tells you Gemini’s growth is coming from reach rather than from users paying for premium tiers.
Claude’s consumer numbers look small next to ChatGPT and Gemini: 245 million monthly active users and 10.3% of the assistant market in May 2026.
The research firm counts Australia’s total AI user base at more than 17 million people, with 80% of them engaging monthly rather than trying a tool once and dropping it.

OpenAI’s weekly active users crossed 900 million on February 27, 2026, and monthly active users passed 1 billion in June 2026, making ChatGPT the fastest app in history to reach that milestone, according to Sensor Tower data reported by TechCrunch.
Annualized revenue crossed $25 billion by February 2026, up from roughly $20 billion in 2025 and $6 billion in 2024.
Mobile app revenue alone hit $1.35 billion in 2025, up 673% year over year from $174 million in 2024.

Roughly $25 billion in annualized revenue against 1.1 billion monthly users works out to an implied $20-something per user per year, though the real split is far more concentrated: a smaller base of paying subscribers and enterprise API customers accounts for most of that revenue, not the free-tier majority.

Analytics provider Apptopia, first reported by Big Technology and later covered by Fortune , tracked ChatGPT’s app market share falling from 69.1% in January 2025 to 45.3% earlier in 2026, while Gemini’s app share rose from 14.7% to 25.2% across the same window. The shift shows up just as clearly in Australia. ChatGPT’s share of the market is shrinking while its user base and revenue keep climbing, because the overall AI-assistant market is expanding faster than ChatGPT alone can capture.

OpenAI Financials Leaked Ahead Of IPO? ChatGPT Maker Said To Have Lost $39B Last Year: Here's How That Compares To Anthropic, SpaceX

OpenAI spent $34 billion on various expenses last year, according to a Financial Times report.

OpenAI’s net loss widened from $5 billion in 2024 to about $39 billion in 2025, the Financial Times reported.

Excluding restructuring charges and other non-cash items, the company’s loss was $8 billion.

OpenAI said in March it was clocking $2 billion in monthly revenue, and Anthropic said last month that it had achieved an annual revenue run rate of $47 billion.

Anthropic’s expenditure and losses are unknown, but the Claude developer said it would report an operating profit of $559 million in the June quarter.

In March, OpenAI raised $122 billion in a funding round at a valuation of $730 billion, excluding the new investment.

Its post-money valuation came out to be $852 billion, trailing Anthropic’s $965 billion valuation.

Last week, Elon Musk’s SpaceX (which includes Musk’s AI business, xAI) listed its shares on Nasdaq in a record-shattering IPO that raised $75 billion.

SpaceX's revenue jumped 33% to $18.67 billion in 2025, but the company swung to a net loss of $4.94 billion from a profit of $791 million, according to its IPO prospectus.

Goldman has estimated ​that ⁠SpaceX's revenue would exceed $470 billion in 2030, while Morgan Stanley projected it would reach nearly $330 ⁠billion.

Reuters and other outlets previously reported that the AI giant could target a valuation of up to $1 trillion in a stock market debut as early as September.

As OpenAI’s value rose, the increased value of those investor rights resulted in a roughly $30 billion charge, according to the FT source.

According to Nasdaq Private Market, OpenAI’s valuation was last at $833.7 billion.

summaryLinesEn: Moonshot's valuation had already increased from $4.3 billion in December to $20 billion within five months, supported by investors including IDG Capital, Alibaba, Meituan, a Chinese food-delivery and local-services company, and several major Chinese state funds.

For investors, Moonshot's recovery could strengthen interest in China's open-source AI sector, while its rapid valuation growth and rising revenue expectations may intensify comparisons with DeepSeek and other Chinese developers competing with OpenAI and Anthropic.
Following the Kimi K3 release, Moonshot's daily sales rose by at least six times, forcing the company to temporarily stop accepting new subscriptions because of limited computing capacity.

Autonomous Threat Detection accounted for nearly 30% of Agentic AI in Cybersecurity capability spending in 2025, highlighting its critical role in modern security operations.

Global cyber incidents are estimated to create around USD 500 billion in annual economic impact, including direct losses, business recovery costs, and additional cybersecurity investments, encouraging enterprises to adopt faster and more automated detection solutions.

Due to limited resources, approximately 40% of security alerts remain uninvestigated, creating demand for AI-powered detection systems that can automatically analyze threats and prioritize critical risks.

Organizations implementing security AI and automation extensively can reduce breach costs by approximately USD 1.9 million per incident and shorten breach lifecycles by 80 days , demonstrating the financial benefits of autonomous detection capabilities.

SOC Automation accounted for an estimated 32.0% of the Agentic AI in Cybersecurity Market by application in 2025, highlighting its critical role in addressing the growing gap between increasing cyber threats and limited Security Operations Center (SOC) resources.

sourceContent.headline: AI is deployed in 57% of enterprises, but only 11% have hit their top two goals
sourceContent.description: Kyndryl's 2026 study of 1,100 leaders finds 57% have deployed AI broadly, yet only 11% have hit both top goals and workforce readiness is falling.
paragraphs: The deployment of AI technology in enterprises has reached 57%, yet only 11% have achieved their primary objectives according to Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report.

While 61% have redesigned roles to support AI adoption and 24% are creating new AI-focused management positions, only one-third have fully implemented employee training programs focused on working alongside AI tools.
Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.
Worldwide AI spending is forecast to reach $2.52 trillion in 2026, a 44% year-over-year increase, according to Gartner research cited in Kyndryl's report.

The Achievers Workforce Institute 's seventh annual State of Recognition Report, cited by MarketScale, found that just 19% of workers feel confident using AI tools, and only 18% feel supported in adapting to them.
Kyndryl's report isolates a cohort it calls Pacesetters: roughly 9% of respondents that are generating measurable AI returns.
Kyndryl's data shows 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful business decisions within the next year.
Half of leaders surveyed, 52%, say it has become more challenging to find employees with the right skills to advance their AI strategy, according to the Kyndryl report.

Pressure-test your agentic AI plans against your current oversight model: 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful decisions within a year, but only 25% fully trust AI without human oversight, making oversight architecture a critical gap to close before autonomous systems go live.

Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.
sourceContent.text:
The deployment of AI technology in enterprises has reached 57%, yet only 11% have achieved their primary objectives according to Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report.

While 61% have redesigned roles to support AI adoption and 24% are creating new AI-focused management positions, only one-third have fully implemented employee training programs focused on working alongside AI tools.

Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.

Worldwide AI spending is forecast to reach $2.52 trillion in 2026, a 44% year-over-year increase, according to Gartner research cited in Kyndryl's report.

The Achievers Workforce Institute 's seventh annual State of Recognition Report, cited by MarketScale, found that just 19% of workers feel confident using AI tools, and only 18% feel supported in adapting to them.

Kyndryl's report isolates a cohort it calls Pacesetters: roughly 9% of respondents that are generating measurable AI returns.

Kyndryl's data shows 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful business decisions within the next year.

Half of leaders surveyed, 52%, say it has become more challenging to find employees with the right skills to advance their AI strategy, according to the Kyndryl report.

Pressure-test your agentic AI plans against your current oversight model: 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful decisions within a year, but only 25% fully trust AI without human oversight, making oversight architecture a critical gap to close before autonomous systems go live.

Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.

sourceContent.headline: Steam AI Disclosure Hits 20% of Games as Rivals Skip [2026]
sourceContent.description: Steam's AI disclosure policy covers 1 in 5 new releases in 2026. Epic, PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo still have no equivalent rule.
paragraphs: By the first half of 2025, close to 8,000 games had filed an AI disclosure on Steam, up from roughly 1,000 across all of 2024, an eightfold jump in about eighteen months.
The jump from roughly 1,000 disclosed games in 2024 to 8,000 by the first half of 2025 shows how fast generative tools moved from novelty to normal practice in PC game development.
A studio leaning on an AI coding assistant to speed up development does not need to say so on its store page.
Steam controls an estimated 74% to 75% of PC digital game distribution by revenue.
Steam’s own record $11.1 billion in first-half 2026 revenue gives the disclosure numbers extra weight.

Steam holds an estimated 74% market share against Epic’s roughly 3% in PC digital distribution, so the platform setting the strictest rule is also the one developers have the least practical ability to avoid.

sourceContent.headline: AI is deployed in 57% of enterprises, but only 11% have hit their top two goals
sourceContent.description: Kyndryl's 2026 study of 1,100 leaders finds 57% have deployed AI broadly, yet only 11% have hit both top goals and workforce readiness is falling.
paragraphs: The deployment of AI technology in enterprises has reached 57%, yet only 11% have achieved their primary objectives according to Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report.

While 61% have redesigned roles to support AI adoption and 24% are creating new AI-focused management positions, only one-third have fully implemented employee training programs focused on working alongside AI tools.
Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.
Worldwide AI spending is forecast to reach $2.52 trillion in 2026, a 44% year-over-year increase, according to Gartner research cited in Kyndryl's report.

The Achievers Workforce Institute 's seventh annual State of Recognition Report, cited by MarketScale, found that just 19% of workers feel confident using AI tools, and only 18% feel supported in adapting to them.
Kyndryl's report isolates a cohort it calls Pacesetters: roughly 9% of respondents that are generating measurable AI returns.
Kyndryl's data shows 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful business decisions within the next year.
Half of leaders surveyed, 52%, say it has become more challenging to find employees with the right skills to advance their AI strategy, according to the Kyndryl report.

Pressure-test your agentic AI plans against your current oversight model: 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful decisions within a year, but only 25% fully trust AI without human oversight, making oversight architecture a critical gap to close before autonomous systems go live.

Home ➤ Information and Communications Technology ➤ Artificial Intelligence ➤ Artificial Intelligence (AI) Market Revenue, 2025 (US$B) 244.3 Bn Forecast, 2035 (US$B) 3520.9 Bn CAGR 2026-2035 30.6% Leading Region North America This report has been updated 2 times .
Last updated on August 3, 2026 78% of organizations reported using AI in 2024, increasing from 55% in 2023, showing rapid movement from experimentation toward operational adoption.
More than 1 million businesses were using OpenAI business products, with ChatGPT Enterprise seats increasing approximately 9× year-over-year.
In 2025 , the Artificial Intelligence Market was valued at USD 244.3 billion .
The market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 30.6% during 2026–2035 , reaching approximately USD 3520.9 billion by 2035 .
North America dominated the global market in 2025, accounting for more than 38.0% of the total market share and generating approximately USD 92.9 billion in revenue.
In 2024, private AI investment in the United States reached USD 109.1 billion , nearly 12 times higher than China’s USD 9.3 billion .
Global spending on AI infrastructure increased from USD 153 billion in 2024 to USD 318 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 487 billion in 2026.

With more than 30–40% of businesses worldwide already using AI in at least one function, wider adoption across healthcare, manufacturing, transport, and public services is expected to support long-term market growth.
Hardware dominated the component segment with a 35% share, driven by rising demand for AI chips, servers, memory, and networking infrastructure.
Cloud-based deployment accounted for a leading 62% share, supported by flexible access to computing power without heavy upfront infrastructure investment.
Machine Learning held a dominant 38% share, supported by broad adoption across banking, manufacturing, healthcare, retail, and professional services.
North America led the global AI market in 2025 with a 38.0% share , generating approximately USD 92.9 billion in revenue.
Hardware held the dominant position in the AI market with a 35% share, supported by the growing need for high-performance chips, servers, memory, and networking equipment.
According to the Semiconductor Industry Association, global semiconductor sales reached USD 627.6 billion in 2024, while logic chip sales, including AI accelerators such as GPUs, increased by 81% .

Department of Commerce also committed USD 39 billion in manufacturing incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act, supporting more than USD 450 billion in announced private semiconductor investments across 28 U.S. states by mid-2024.
Electronics manufacturing represented 58% of U.S. manufacturing construction, reaching an annualized USD 135 billion in June 2024.
In 2025, AI represented about 61% of global venture capital investment value, supporting continued growth in scalable, subscription-based AI software.

Cloud-based deployment held the dominant position in the AI market with a 62% share, mainly because it allows organizations to access advanced computing power without spending tens of millions of dollars on dedicated GPU infrastructure.
Global cloud infrastructure spending reached USD 95.3 billion , increasing by 22% year over year.
AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud collectively accounted for 65% of the market.

Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta invested a combined USD 248 billion in capital expenditure during 2024, with spending projected to exceed USD 300 billion in 2025, largely supporting AI-focused data centers and cloud infrastructure.
OECD data showed that the share of firms actively using AI increased from 8.7% in 2023 to 14.2% in 2024 and reached 20.2% in 2025.
The BFSI sector held the dominant position in the AI market with a 20% share, supported by its high dependence on data, automation, security, and regulatory compliance.
The sector manages an estimated USD 120 trillion in global assets under management, creating strong demand for AI systems that improve accuracy, reduce costs, and support faster decisions.
According to the World Health Organization, global healthcare spending per person increased by more than 60% between 2000 and 2022.

paragraphs: Total revenue reached $28.24 billion, up 26% year-over-year and surpassing the $25.71 billion average analyst estimate surveyed by LSEG.
Despite financial pressures, Tesla's core auto sales business showed strong recovery momentum in the second quarter.

Even as vehicle deliveries hit a record high and drove substantial revenue growth, the company burned through nearly $5.8 billion in just 90 days—sacrificing profits and cash flow to build the massive infrastructure needed to support artificial intelligence and humanoid robots.
Tesla Posts Record Q2 Revenue But Swings to Loss, Burns $5.8 Billion in 90 Days Betting on AI and Humanoid Robot Infrastructure — BigGo Finance
Following the release, Tesla shares fell more than 3% in after-hours trading as earnings missed expectations and free cash flow turned negative.

The revenue growth was primarily driven by a strong rebound in global deliveries, with Tesla handing over more than 480,000 pure electric vehicles worldwide during the quarter—a roughly 25% year-over-year increase and a new all-time high.
Net income attributable to common shareholders was $1.114 billion, down 5% from $1.172 billion in the same period last year.
More concerning for investors, adjusted earnings per share came in at just $0.33, significantly below the average analyst estimate of $0.51.
Meanwhile, global carbon credit revenue plummeted to $146 million from $439 million in the prior-year quarter, further weighing on profitability.
In the second quarter, Tesla's capex reached $5.789 billion, surging 142% year-over-year.
By this measure, Tesla spent roughly $64.32 million per day over the past 90 days.
The massive outlay directly resulted in negative free cash flow of $1.092 billion—the first such occurrence in more than two years.
Musk has raised this year's capital expenditure forecast to over $25 billion, nearly triple last year's $8.5 billion.
Notably, actual spending in the first half reached $8.3 billion, meaning nearly $17 billion must be spent in the second half to fulfill the commitment.
Total automotive revenue for the period was $20.516 billion, up 23% year-over-year.
Among these, combined deliveries of the Model 3 and Model Y reached 467,762 units, a 25% increase, remaining the absolute workhorses.
The Model Y has held the title of the world's best-selling vehicle for three consecutive years, with cumulative sales now exceeding 4 million units.
First-half deliveries totaled nearly 468,000 units, up 28.4% year-over-year.
In Europe, the Model Y became the best-selling pure electric model in May with monthly sales exceeding 17,000 units.

In the Asia-Pacific market, Model Y sales in Australia skyrocketed 133.5% year-over-year, making it the best-selling vehicle across all categories in the local market for the second consecutive month.
In the robotaxi space, the Cybercab—a fully autonomous electric vehicle—has entered production at the Texas Gigafactory, with a designed annual capacity exceeding 125,000 units.

With the official retirement of the Model S and Model X production lines at the Fremont factory, the vacated space has begun installing Optimus's first-generation production line, with a planned annual capacity of 1 million units.
Meanwhile, a second production line at the Texas Gigafactory is already in preparation, with a long-term designed annual capacity of up to 10 million units.
On the assisted driving software front, FSD's global paid subscriber base has reached 1.48 million, with over half of new vehicles delivered in the North American market subscribing to the service.

As nearly $17 billion in second-half capital expenditure plans gradually materialize, the market will be watching closely to see whether this enormous investment can truly fortify its physical-world AI moat.

This dynamic is accelerating growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised models, which are forecast to grow 210 percent in 2026.

Gartner predicts AI models and platforms spend to hit US$64B

Spending on generative AI (genAI) models is forecast to grow 117 per cent while AI platform spending will rise 36.9 per cent in 2026, according to Gartner’s latest forecast on AI platforms and models. “Enterprise AI budgets are coming under greater scrutiny, with increased focus on usage efficiency, cost control and measurable outcomes ,” said the analyst firm’s senior principal research analyst, Arunasree Cheparthi. “Spending is shifting toward providers who can demonstrate clear value across cost, latency, performance, and reliability. “This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency, and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use.” However, as spending becomes more usage-driven, providers face pressure to demonstrate real adoption, sustained use, and durable margins.

According to Gartner, the AI software market is forecast to grow significantly between 2025 and 2026, with total market revenue increasing from US$39.3 billion to US$64.3 billion, representing 63.4 per cent growth.
Meanwhile, the fastest-growing segment is DSLMs and specialised genAI models, which is projected to expand from US$1.6 billion to US$4.9 billion, achieving 210.0 per cent growth.

AI application development platforms are forecast to grow from US$6.9 billion to US$9.5 billion (up 38.6 per cent), and AI platforms for data science and machine learning are expected to increase from US$19.4 billion to US$26.4 billion (an increase of 36.3 per cent).

Worldwide end-user spending on AI models and platforms is projected to total US$64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from US$39 billion in 2025, with more and more enterprises are choosing to work with companies that can provide clear value. This dynamic is accelerating growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised models, which are forecast to grow 210 percent in 2026. The Foundation Generative AI Models segment is expected to more than double, rising from US$11.4 billion in 2025 to US$23.4 billion in 2026, representing a growth rate of 104.2 per cent.
