sourceContent.headline: ERP Software Market
sourceContent.description: By 2035, the ERP Software Market is projected to reach USD 231.1 Bn, up from USD 82.2 Bn in 2025, at a CAGR of 10.9%.
paragraphs: According to the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), global software spending reached approximately USD 675 billion in 2024, increasing by nearly 50% from USD 454 billion in 2020.
Cloud ERP adoption is accelerating as organizations seek lower upfront costs, faster deployment, scalability, and reduced infrastructure requirements.
This growth reflects the shift of businesses from traditional processes toward software-based solutions that improve automation, efficiency, and decision-making.
Revenue 2025 (US$B) 82.2 Bn Forecast 2035 (US$B) 231.1 Bn CAGR 2026-2035 10.9% Leading Region Asia Pacific This report has been updated 2 times .
Last updated on July 16, 2026 Around 70% of large enterprises use ERP systems to manage core business processes, including finance, supply chain, and human resources.
Around 64% of ERP implementation projects require more than 6 months to complete from initiation to go-live.
Approximately 53% of organizations report achieving a positive return on investment (ROI) from their ERP implementations.
In 2025, the Global ERP software market was valued at USD 82.2 billion and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.9% from 2026 to 2035, reaching around USD 231.1 billion by 2035.

The Asia-Pacific region holds a leading position, accounting for more than 36.78% of global ERP revenues, supported by rapid digital transformation , strong manufacturing and services industries, and increasing enterprise technology investments.
Additionally, Asia-Pacific ICT spending is projected to reach around USD 1.4 trillion in 2025, showing strong investment in IT infrastructure and enterprise applications.
The Global ERP Software Market was valued at USD 82.2 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 231.1 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 10.9% during 2026 to 2035.
On-premises deployment dominates the market with a 68.78% share, driven by enterprise preference for control, security, and customized infrastructure.
Finance function holds the largest share among ERP applications, accounting for 31.67% due to increasing demand for integrated financial management solutions.
Large enterprises represent the leading enterprise size segment with a 67.67% share, supported by complex operational requirements and higher technology investments.
Retail vertical dominates ERP adoption with a 48.67% share, driven by the need for inventory management, supply chain optimization, and customer operations integration.
Asia-Pacific leads the ERP Software Market with a 36.78% share, generating approximately USD 30.21 billion in market revenue.

In 2024, global manufacturing value added reached about USD 16.8 trillion , representing a substantial share of world GDP and reflecting millions of factory-floor operations that depend on tightly coupled, low-latency ERP, MES, and production control systems hosted on local infrastructure for deterministic performance and uptime.

In parallel, banking institutions manage more than USD 180 trillion in assets worldwide, embedding ERP into highly regulated finance and risk platforms where data residency, encryption control, and audited change management favor in-house hosting.

The Finance function segment, with a dominant 31.67% share of the ERP software market by function, leads adoption because it is directly tied to statutory financial reporting and tax compliance across virtually all formal enterprises worldwide.

Small and medium enterprises represent about 90% of all businesses and over 50% of employment globally, yet every one of these firms must maintain compliant accounts and file corporate taxes, which on average contribute 17.8% of total tax revenues across 131 jurisdictions according to OECD Corporate Tax Statistics 2025.

IFRS Accounting Standards are required or permitted in more than 140 jurisdictions, and IOSCO members regulate over 95% of the world’s securities markets, creating a unified global framework that demands granular, auditable financial data captured and consolidated through ERP finance modules.
Large Enterprises , which account for approximately 67.6% of ERP software revenues by enterprise size, dominate the market because they sit at the center of global value creation and trade.
The world’s 500 largest corporations alone generated about 41 to 41.7 trillion USD in revenue in 2023 to 2024, equivalent to roughly one-third of global GDP and employing over 70 million people.
The Retail Vertical, accounting for 48.67% of ERP software demand, justifiably holds the dominant share of the ERP software market.

Its scale alone creates a structural need for advanced ERP: the wholesale and retail trade sector employs about 420.5 million people worldwide, making it one of the largest global employers and a major generator of transactional and inventory data.

UNCTAD estimates total global e-commerce sales at roughly USD 26.7 trillion , with online retail sales growing three times faster than overall retail between 2017 and 2023, sharply increasing data, order, and fulfillment complexity for retailers.

ERP software directly addresses these pain points by consolidating point-of-sale , inventory, supply chain, and financials into a single, real-time system of record, which is economically critical in a low-margin sector where even a 1 to 2% productivity or shrinkage improvement materially lifts profit.

Cloud ERP adoption is accelerating as organizations seek lower upfront costs, faster deployment, scalability, and reduced infrastructure requirements.

Around 64% of ERP implementation projects require more than 6 months to complete from initiation to go-live.

Approximately 53% of organizations report achieving a positive return on investment (ROI) from their ERP implementations.

In 2025, the Global ERP software market was valued at USD 82.2 billion and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.9% from 2026 to 2035, reaching around USD 231.1 billion by 2035.

The Asia-Pacific region holds a leading position, accounting for more than 36.78% of global ERP revenues, supported by rapid digital transformation , strong manufacturing and services industries, and increasing enterprise technology investments.

Additionally, Asia-Pacific ICT spending is projected to reach around USD 1.4 trillion in 2025, showing strong investment in IT infrastructure and enterprise applications.

The Global ERP Software Market was valued at USD 82.2 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 231.1 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 10.9% during 2026 to 2035.

On-premises deployment dominates the market with a 68.78% share, driven by enterprise preference for control, security, and customized infrastructure.

Finance function holds the largest share among ERP applications, accounting for 31.67% due to increasing demand for integrated financial management solutions.

Large enterprises represent the leading enterprise size segment with a 67.67% share, supported by complex operational requirements and higher technology investments.

Retail vertical dominates ERP adoption with a 48.67% share, driven by the need for inventory management, supply chain optimization, and customer operations integration.

Asia-Pacific leads the ERP Software Market with a 36.78% share, generating approximately USD 30.21 billion in market revenue.

In 2024, global manufacturing value added reached about USD 16.8 trillion , representing a substantial share of world GDP and reflecting millions of factory-floor operations that depend on tightly coupled, low-latency ERP, MES, and production control systems hosted on local infrastructure for deterministic performance and uptime.

In parallel, banking institutions manage more than USD 180 trillion in assets worldwide, embedding ERP into highly regulated finance and risk platforms where data residency, encryption control, and audited change management favor in-house hosting.

The Finance function segment, with a dominant 31.67% share of the ERP software market by function, leads adoption because it is directly tied to statutory financial reporting and tax compliance across virtually all formal enterprises worldwide.

Small and medium enterprises represent about 90% of all businesses and over 50% of employment globally, yet every one of these firms must maintain compliant accounts and file corporate taxes, which on average contribute 17.8% of total tax revenues across 131 jurisdictions according to OECD Corporate Tax Statistics 2025.

IFRS Accounting Standards are required or permitted in more than 140 jurisdictions, and IOSCO members regulate over 95% of the world’s securities markets, creating a unified global framework that demands granular, auditable financial data captured and consolidated through ERP finance modules.

Large Enterprises , which account for approximately 67.6% of ERP software revenues by enterprise size, dominate the market because they sit at the center of global value creation and trade.

The world’s 500 largest corporations alone generated about 41 to 41.7 trillion USD in revenue in 2023 to 2024, equivalent to roughly one-third of global GDP and employing over 70 million people.

The Retail Vertical, accounting for 48.67% of ERP software demand, justifiably holds the dominant share of the ERP software market.

Its scale alone creates a structural need for advanced ERP: the wholesale and retail trade sector employs about 420.5 million people worldwide, making it one of the largest global employers and a major generator of transactional and inventory data.

UNCTAD estimates total global e-commerce sales at roughly USD 26.7 trillion , with online retail sales growing three times faster than overall retail between 2017 and 2023, sharply increasing data, order, and fulfillment complexity for retailers.

ERP software directly addresses these pain points by consolidating point-of-sale , inventory, supply chain, and financials into a single, real-time system of record, which is economically critical in a low-margin sector where even a 1 to 2% productivity or shrinkage improvement materially lifts profit.

The global cloud ERP segment is expanding at nearly 20% annual growth , supported by increasing demand for subscription-based enterprise solutions.

Cloud ERP implementations have become approximately 40% faster than traditional on-premise deployments, reducing adoption barriers for businesses.

This growth reflects the shift of businesses from traditional processes toward software-based solutions that improve automation, efficiency, and decision-making.

sourceContent.headline: Enterprise AI Adoption: 59% Spend $1M+, 29% See ROI [2026] - tech-insider.org
sourceContent.description: 59% of firms now spend $1M+ yearly on enterprise AI adoption, but only 29% see real ROI. See the 2026 data and how Canada compares to the US.
paragraphs: The clearest picture of the spending-versus-results gap comes from WRITER’s 2026 AI Adoption in the Enterprise survey , fielded between December 17, 2025 and January 25, 2026.

The Productivity Paradox: 5x Personal Gains, 29% Company ROI Canada vs. the United States: A Smaller, Slower ROI Curve Market Impact: What the ROI Gap Means for Vendors and Buyers Competitive Comparison: How OpenAI, Microsoft, Google and Anthropic Are Responding What Comes Next: 5 Predictions for Enterprise AI Spending That gap between AI spending and AI payoff has become the defining budget fight inside technology departments this year.

Canadian businesses more than tripled their use of artificial intelligence in two years, moving from 6.1% adoption in the second quarter of 2024 to 19.2% by the same period in 2026, according to Statistics Canada.
Enterprise AI Adoption: 59% Spend $1M+, 29% See ROI [2026] - tech-insider.org
Globally the pattern looks even sharper: 59% of organizations now spend at least $1 million a year on AI, based on a WRITER-commissioned survey of 2,400 executives and employees published in 2026.

Workplace Intelligence polled 2,400 people on WRITER’s behalf: 1,200 C-suite executives and 1,200 employees at companies ranging from 100 to more than 10,000 workers, spread across nearly 30 industries in the United States, United Kingdom, Ireland, the Benelux region, France, and Germany.
Fifty-nine percent of companies now invest $1 million or more annually in AI technology.

And in a finding that should worry any finance team, 54% of C-suite respondents said AI adoption is tearing their company apart internally, the product of fights over budget ownership, tool sprawl, and who decides which model powers which workflow.
The same WRITER research found that 67% of executives believe their company has already suffered a data breach tied to unapproved, employee-installed AI tools, a pattern often called shadow AI.
Seventy-nine percent of organizations now call AI a strategic priority, up from 74% in the first quarter, and 22% classify AI as simply part of everyday work, up from 13% the quarter before.
Average AI spending among surveyed organizations reached $188 million.
Despite that scale of investment, just 7% of organizations told KPMG they had established measurable ROI on their AI spending.

Twenty-four percent of organizations say they struggle specifically with managing usage-based AI costs, and 49% have already delayed or scaled back an AI initiative after its cost exceeded its measured value.
Companies with 100 or more employees report 27.8% adoption, compared with 19.9% among the smallest businesses.
Urban firms sit at 21.0% adoption versus 9.9% in rural areas.
Information and cultural industries lead the country at 42.3% adoption, followed by finance and insurance at 40.4% and professional, scientific, and technical services at 32.4%.

Statistics Canada also found that 44.4% of businesses using AI made training or staffing changes as a direct result, evidence that adoption is reshaping headcount decisions well before most companies have settled the ROI question.
For more on the policy side of that push, see our coverage of Canada’s $200 billion national AI strategy and how it aims to accelerate adoption in the sectors currently lagging.
Sixty-nine percent of Canadian firms report partial or full AI integration, compared with 89% in the United States.
On returns, 43% of Canadian companies say their AI investments have exceeded ROI expectations, against 57% of American companies.
On spending intentions, only 41% of Canadian firms plan to invest $1 million or more in AI this fiscal year, versus 62% south of the border.

The clearest picture of the spending-versus-results gap comes from WRITER’s 2026 AI Adoption in the Enterprise survey , fielded between December 17, 2025 and January 25, 2026. paragraphs: Meta Platforms reported strong revenue and user growth in Q2 2026 while increasing investment in AI infrastructure.
Meta launched Meta One, which combines additional features and AI tools for consumers, businesses and creators, with plans for multiple subscription tiers and pricing options.
Meta’s Reality Labs generated $431 million in Q2 revenue, up 16 percent, primarily due to strong growth in AI glasses revenue, partly offset by lower Quest headset sales.
Meta Q2 2026 Revenue Jumps 28% to $60.8 bn as AI Capex Reaches $31.1 bn and User Base Hits 3.6 bn - InfotechLead
Quarterly revenue of Meta Platforms has reached $60.8 billion, up 28 percent.
Operating income was $18.8 billion, down 8 percent, with an operating margin of 31 percent, while net income reached $15.8 billion, or $6.18 per share.
Meta’s global customer base continued expanding, with 3.6 billion people using at least one Meta app every day.
Instagram reached 2 billion daily active users, while Threads crossed 500 million monthly active users.
Facebook remained above 2 billion daily active users.
WhatsApp also recorded a peak of 30 million messages per second during the FIFA 2026 World Cup Final.
Family of Apps other revenue reached $1 billion for the first time, growing 73 percent, primarily driven by WhatsApp paid messaging and subscription revenue.

This gives Meta two very different business engines: its roughly $60.4 billion Family of Apps operation and the much smaller $431 million Reality Labs division, where AI glasses represent an increasingly important growth opportunity.

$31.1 Billion Quarterly Investment in AI Infrastructure Meta’s capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, surged to $31.1 billion in Q2, primarily reflecting investment in servers, data centers and network infrastructure.
Meta narrowed its full-year 2026 capex forecast to $130 billion-$145 billion, compared with its previous $125 billion-$145 billion range.
AI Business Agents Reach More Than 1 Million Businesses Meta is rapidly converting AI investment into enterprise products.
More than 1 million businesses are already using Meta Business Agents every week on WhatsApp and Messenger to communicate with customers or complete sales.

Its WhatsApp AI Business Agent helped generate a 44 percent year-over-year increase in daily bookings during a one-month period, while 85 percent of conversations were resolved entirely by AI without human assistance.
Following the rebuilding of Meta AI and integration of Muse Spark, the number of people interacting with the assistant each day increased 60 percent.
Instagram time spent increased double digits, while Facebook video time grew 9 percent globally and more than 10 percent in the U.S. and Canada.

Meta Platforms reported strong revenue and user growth in Q2 2026 while increasing investment in AI infrastructure.

Meta launched Meta One, which combines additional features and AI tools for consumers, businesses and creators, with plans for multiple subscription tiers and pricing options.

Meta’s Reality Labs generated $431 million in Q2 revenue, up 16 percent, primarily due to strong growth in AI glasses revenue, partly offset by lower Quest headset sales.

Meta Q2 2026 Revenue Jumps 28% to $60.8 bn as AI Capex Reaches $31.1 bn and User Base Hits 3.6 bn - InfotechLead

Quarterly revenue of Meta Platforms has reached $60.8 billion, up 28 percent.

Operating income was $18.8 billion, down 8 percent, with an operating margin of 31 percent, while net income reached $15.8 billion, or $6.18 per share.

Meta’s global customer base continued expanding, with 3.6 billion people using at least one Meta app every day.

Instagram reached 2 billion daily active users, while Threads crossed 500 million monthly active users.

Facebook remained above 2 billion daily active users.

WhatsApp also recorded a peak of 30 million messages per second during the FIFA 2026 World Cup Final.

Family of Apps other revenue reached $1 billion for the first time, growing 73 percent, primarily driven by WhatsApp paid messaging and subscription revenue.

This gives Meta two very different business engines: its roughly $60.4 billion Family of Apps operation and the much smaller $431 million Reality Labs division, where AI glasses represent an increasingly important growth opportunity.

$31.1 Billion Quarterly Investment in AI Infrastructure Meta’s capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, surged to $31.1 billion in Q2, primarily reflecting investment in servers, data centers and network infrastructure.

Meta narrowed its full-year 2026 capex forecast to $130 billion-$145 billion, compared with its previous $125 billion-$145 billion range.

AI Business Agents Reach More Than 1 Million Businesses Meta is rapidly converting AI investment into enterprise products.

More than 1 million businesses are already using Meta Business Agents every week on WhatsApp and Messenger to communicate with customers or complete sales.

Its WhatsApp AI Business Agent helped generate a 44 percent year-over-year increase in daily bookings during a one-month period, while 85 percent of conversations were resolved entirely by AI without human assistance.

Following the rebuilding of Meta AI and integration of Muse Spark, the number of people interacting with the assistant each day increased 60 percent.

Instagram time spent increased double digits, while Facebook video time grew 9 percent globally and more than 10 percent in the U.S. and Canada.

DRAM Prices Could Rise 13–18 Percent as Memory Crisis Hits Rivals Apple’s market-share expansion is taking place against a challenging component-cost environment.

sourceLines: Counterpoint forecasts Apple will increase shipment share across all four major device categories in 2026. iPad share is projected to rise from 35 percent in 2025 to 39 percent in 2026, iPhone from 23 percent to 25 percent, Mac from 9 percent to 12 percent and Apple Watch from 20 percent to 23 percent.
Apple introduced the M5-powered iPad Pro in late 2025, followed by an updated iPad Air earlier in 2026.
Demand for the standard iPhone 17 is also expected to remain healthy because Apple is not anticipated to introduce a regular iPhone 18 model during 2026.

records.evidence:
Valid responses totaled 10,000 for the screening survey and 3,300 for the main survey.
Its first survey, titled "Consumer AI Usage Survey 2026.7," examined how AI is being used in purchasing behavior and decision-making.
Dentsu Digital said the findings show AI use is spreading in awareness, comparison and post-purchase phases, while people still account for a higher share of decision-making at the final stage.

Dentsu Digital said the findings show AI use is spreading in awareness, comparison and post-purchase phases, while people still account for a higher share of decision-making at the final stage.
Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning

Dentsu Digital launches with AI Lab and publishes a July 2026 survey on consumer AI use in purchasing About one in three private AI users consult AI before purchases, with travel and financial categories above 50% AI use is strongest in awareness, comparison and post-purchase stages, while final buying decisions remain more human-led Dentsu Digital said on July 23 that about one in three consumers who use artificial intelligence in their private lives had consulted AI about purchases made within the past six months, releasing the first findings from a new in-house research unit focused on consumer behavior in the AI era.

The ratio was highest in higher-involvement categories where consumers tend to compare options more closely, with 57% in travel planning and accommodation bookings and 56% in financial products and insurance.

Across product categories, 2% to 3% of respondents said they adopted AI responses as-is for their final decision, indicating that some consumers are beginning to leave the ultimate purchase choice to AI.

localization.title: Dentsu Digital 조사에 따르면 57%가 여행 계획에 AI를 사용하는 것으로 나타남
summaryLines: 유효 응답자는 선별 조사에서 10,000명, 본 조사에서 3,300명이었음
'소비자 AI 사용 설문조사 2026.7'이라는 제목의 첫 번째 설문조사에서는 AI가 구매 행동 및 의사 결정에 어떻게 사용되는지 조사함
Dentsu Digital은 연구 결과에 따르면 AI 사용이 인식, 비교 및 구매 후 단계에서 확산되고 있는 반면 최종 단계에서는 여전히 사람들이 의사 결정에서 더 높은 비중을 차지하고 있음을 보여줌

sourceContent.headline: DoubleVerify: ad fraud drops 41% in North America, 45% in EMEA
sourceContent.description: AI bots generated ten times more clicks than humans in unprotected campaigns, DoubleVerify found, as marketers weigh growing risks from generative AI content.
paragraphs: In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate dropped 41 percent compared with 2024, though the region still posted the highest rate of any market DoubleVerify tracks, at 0.6 percent, driven mainly by the United States.
EMEA marketers instead prioritized the ability to review or approve AI-generated creatives, at 38 percent, ahead of data-privacy safeguards.

The company derives its wasted-spend estimates by multiplying total violations by an assumed cost per mille of 3 dollars, a figure the report applies uniformly across markets despite considerable variation in actual media pricing between, for instance, the United States and other markets in the same region.
by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

Reach out via luis@ppc.land LinkedIn DoubleVerify today released regional editions of its 2026 Global Insights report, "Media Quality in the Age of AI," reporting that fraud and invalid traffic violation rates fell 41 percent year over year in North America and 45 percent in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, while artificial intelligence bots generated up to ten times more clicks than humans in some unprotected ad campaigns.
The Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate fell 45 percent year over year, continuing what DoubleVerify describes as the world's lowest regional rate for the metric.
Non-human data center traffic, the most prevalent fraud type in the region, dropped 54 percent.

Unprotected campaigns, meaning those without DoubleVerify's pre-bid or post-bid safeguards, recorded a fraud violation rate of 2.8 percent globally, compared with 0.6 percent for protected campaigns, a difference the report expresses as 384 percent.

That comparison echoes the structure of DoubleVerify's own Q1 2026 quarterly benchmarks report , which similarly found fraud and SIVT violations falling 24 percent year over year to 0.5 percent globally in that earlier dataset, alongside a rising out-of-geo violation rate that ran counter to the broader trend.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate on desktop stood at 0.9 percent, against 0.8 percent on mobile app and 0.5 percent on mobile web; desktop showed the steepest year-over-year reduction, at 48 percent.

In EMEA, the pattern reversed: mobile app recorded the largest improvement, falling 51 percent to reach a 0.4 percent violation rate, while desktop, at 0.8 percent, improved by 44 percent and mobile web, at 0.2 percent, improved by 49 percent.

The lab found that in unprotected media, AI bots generated 15 percent of clicks across the campaigns studied, and that in some individual studies, a monitored ad click was ten times more likely to come from a bot than from a human.

A State of Click Fraud Report published by Lunio in July 2026 found that 75.6 percent of surveyed marketers estimated losing more than 5 percent of their monthly performance budget to invalid traffic, while only 5.3 percent used a dedicated prevention platform.

North America's Brand Suitability Violation Rate fell to 4.1 percent, a 10 percent year-over-year reduction and the lowest of any region DoubleVerify tracks; the figure has now declined for three consecutive years, from 5.4 percent in 2023 to 4.6 percent in 2024 and 4.1 percent in 2025.

Within North America, the United States recorded a 4 percent violation rate against Canada's 8 percent, though Canada's figure dropped 11 percent year over year compared with a 9 percent reduction in the United States.
EMEA's rate fell only 2 percent, to 6.9 percent, and the region continued to underperform the 4.8 percent global benchmark.

The regional average obscured wide variation by market: France's violation rate dropped sharply, to 4 percent, below the global benchmark, while rates in Italy and Turkey rose year over year, and Eastern Europe recorded the highest subregional rate at 9.9 percent, even as that figure itself fell 14 percent from the prior year.
Globally, unprotected campaigns recorded a 13.8 percent brand suitability violation rate against 4.8 percent for protected campaigns, a gap DoubleVerify expresses as 189 percent.

The report's Vodafone Germany case study found that after implementing DoubleVerify's Authentic Brand Suitability product, the telecommunications company reduced media waste by 79 percent and its block rate by 72 percent, alongside CPM and quality-adjusted CPM reductions of 4 percent and 10 percent respectively.

Similar deployment findings for Vodafone in EMEA news environments appeared in an earlier PPC Land report from July 2025, which found the company had reduced block rates by 41 percent and keyword violations by 48 percent year over year, redirecting the resulting savings into additional purchases of news publisher inventory.
DoubleVerify says its AI SlopStopper tool blocked or monitored more than 500 million impressions across both regions in the first half of 2026 combined.

North American marketers reported far greater reluctance than their global counterparts about using AI to build ad copy and creatives: 63 percent said they were somewhat to very concerned, against a 48 percent global figure.
EMEA marketers showed the opposite pattern, expressing less concern than the global average, at 43 percent against 45 percent globally.

North American marketers proved the most wary of any group in either report about serving ads inside AI platforms, with 63 percent describing themselves as somewhat to very concerned, against a 50 percent global average; EMEA marketers were closer to that global figure, at 47 percent.

Consumer reactions in North America followed a similar pattern, with only the single scenario of "the ad is highly relevant to the chat" producing more positive than negative sentiment, at 31 percent positive against 19 percent negative.
Ads appearing alongside chats the report characterizes as negative or sad drew 34 percent negative sentiment in North America, the least favorable result recorded for any chat scenario tested.
North American marketers ranked transparent reporting on where ads are served and reliable measurement and attribution of ad performance as their top two requirements, both at 39 percent.

North America's overall viewable rate rose 4 percent year over year; video viewability in the United States specifically climbed 10 percent to reach 88 percent, while Canada's video rate rose a more modest 4 percent to 84 percent.

EMEA video viewability rose only 1 percent regionally, to 84 percent, still trailing the 87 percent global benchmark, though France recorded the sharpest single-market improvement in display viewability, up 8 percent to 67 percent.

July 19, 2025 - IAS identifies AI-generated slop sites as a major ad quality threat , finding quality inventory delivers 91 percent higher conversion rates.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate dropped 41 percent compared with 2024, though the region still posted the highest rate of any market DoubleVerify tracks, at 0.6 percent, driven mainly by the United States.

EMEA marketers instead prioritized the ability to review or approve AI-generated creatives, at 38 percent, ahead of data-privacy safeguards.

The company derives its wasted-spend estimates by multiplying total violations by an assumed cost per mille of 3 dollars, a figure the report applies uniformly across markets despite considerable variation in actual media pricing between, for instance, the United States and other markets in the same region.

by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

Reach out via luis@ppc.land LinkedIn DoubleVerify today released regional editions of its 2026 Global Insights report, "Media Quality in the Age of AI," reporting that fraud and invalid traffic violation rates fell 41 percent year over year in North America and 45 percent in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, while artificial intelligence bots generated up to ten times more clicks than humans in some unprotected ad campaigns.

The Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate fell 45 percent year over year, continuing what DoubleVerify describes as the world's lowest regional rate for the metric.

Non-human data center traffic, the most prevalent fraud type in the region, dropped 54 percent.

Unprotected campaigns, meaning those without DoubleVerify's pre-bid or post-bid safeguards, recorded a fraud violation rate of 2.8 percent globally, compared with 0.6 percent for protected campaigns, a difference the report expresses as 384 percent.

That comparison echoes the structure of DoubleVerify's own Q1 2026 quarterly benchmarks report , which similarly found fraud and SIVT violations falling 24 percent year over year to 0.5 percent globally in that earlier dataset, alongside a rising out-of-geo violation rate that ran counter to the broader trend.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate on desktop stood at 0.9 percent, against 0.8 percent on mobile app and 0.5 percent on mobile web; desktop showed the steepest year-over-year reduction, at 48 percent.

In EMEA, the pattern reversed: mobile app recorded the largest improvement, falling 51 percent to reach a 0.4 percent violation rate, while desktop, at 0.8 percent, improved by 44 percent and mobile web, at 0.2 percent, improved by 49 percent.

The lab found that in unprotected media, AI bots generated 15 percent of clicks across the campaigns studied, and that in some individual studies, a monitored ad click was ten times more likely to come from a bot than from a human.

A State of Click Fraud Report published by Lunio in July 2026 found that 75.6 percent of surveyed marketers estimated losing more than 5 percent of their monthly performance budget to invalid traffic, while only 5.3 percent used a dedicated prevention platform.

North America's Brand Suitability Violation Rate fell to 4.1 percent, a 10 percent year-over-year reduction and the lowest of any region DoubleVerify tracks; the figure has now declined for three consecutive years, from 5.4 percent in 2023 to 4.6 percent in 2024 and 4.1 percent in 2025.

Within North America, the United States recorded a 4 percent violation rate against Canada's 8 percent, though Canada's figure dropped 11 percent year over year compared with a 9 percent reduction in the United States.

EMEA's rate fell only 2 percent, to 6.9 percent, and the region continued to underperform the 4.8 percent global benchmark.

The regional average obscured wide variation by market: France's violation rate dropped sharply, to 4 percent, below the global benchmark, while rates in Italy and Turkey rose year over year, and Eastern Europe recorded the highest subregional rate at 9.9 percent, even as that figure itself fell 14 percent from the prior year.

Globally, unprotected campaigns recorded a 13.8 percent brand suitability violation rate against 4.8 percent for protected campaigns, a gap DoubleVerify expresses as 189 percent.

The report's Vodafone Germany case study found that after implementing DoubleVerify's Authentic Brand Suitability product, the telecommunications company reduced media waste by 79 percent and its block rate by 72 percent, alongside CPM and quality-adjusted CPM reductions of 4 percent and 10 percent respectively.

Similar deployment findings for Vodafone in EMEA news environments appeared in an earlier PPC Land report from July 2025, which found the company had reduced block rates by 41 percent and keyword violations by 48 percent year over year, redirecting the resulting savings into additional purchases of news publisher inventory.

DoubleVerify says its AI SlopStopper tool blocked or monitored more than 500 million impressions across both regions in the first half of 2026 combined.

North American marketers reported far greater reluctance than their global counterparts about using AI to build ad copy and creatives: 63 percent said they were somewhat to very concerned, against a 48 percent global figure.

EMEA marketers showed the opposite pattern, expressing less concern than the global average, at 43 percent against 45 percent globally.

North American marketers proved the most wary of any group in either report about serving ads inside AI platforms, with 63 percent describing themselves as somewhat to very concerned, against a 50 percent global average; EMEA marketers were closer to that global figure, at 47 percent.

Consumer reactions in North America followed a similar pattern, with only the single scenario of "the ad is highly relevant to the chat" producing more positive than negative sentiment, at 31 percent positive against 19 percent negative.

Ads appearing alongside chats the report characterizes as negative or sad drew 34 percent negative sentiment in North America, the least favorable result recorded for any chat scenario tested.

North American marketers ranked transparent reporting on where ads are served and reliable measurement and attribution of ad performance as their top two requirements, both at 39 percent.

North America's overall viewable rate rose 4 percent year over year; video viewability in the United States specifically climbed 10 percent to reach 88 percent, while Canada's video rate rose a more modest 4 percent to 84 percent.

EMEA video viewability rose only 1 percent regionally, to 84 percent, still trailing the 87 percent global benchmark, though France recorded the sharpest single-market improvement in display viewability, up 8 percent to 67 percent.

July 19, 2025 - IAS identifies AI-generated slop sites as a major ad quality threat , finding quality inventory delivers 91 percent higher conversion rates.

records.evidence:
According to Yelp, only 48 percent of respondents said they trust AI-generated summaries to be accurate for service professionals, and the figure drops further, to 43 percent, for restaurants.
Four days later, on July 28, 2026, Yelp introduced more than a dozen updates to Yelp Host, its AI-powered phone answering service for restaurants, including a new integration with OpenTable and native food ordering for pickup orders, according to a PPC Land report published at the time .
Why this matters for marketers, publishers, and platforms The 15-percent overall AI trust figure from Yelp's April 2026 Morning Consult research, referenced again in this new study, has become something of a reference point across the trade press precisely because it complicates the assumption that AI adoption and AI trust move in lockstep.

sourceContent.headline: Yelp: only 43% of Gen Z trusts AI summaries for restaurants
sourceContent.description: Survey data covering 1,323 respondents shows 97% of Gen Z research restaurants before spending, while written reviews outrank influencer picks by 19 points.
paragraphs: According to Yelp, only 48 percent of respondents said they trust AI-generated summaries to be accurate for service professionals, and the figure drops further, to 43 percent, for restaurants.

Four days later, on July 28, 2026, Yelp introduced more than a dozen updates to Yelp Host, its AI-powered phone answering service for restaurants, including a new integration with OpenTable and native food ordering for pickup orders, according to a PPC Land report published at the time .

Why this matters for marketers, publishers, and platforms The 15-percent overall AI trust figure from Yelp's April 2026 Morning Consult research, referenced again in this new study, has become something of a reference point across the trade press precisely because it complicates the assumption that AI adoption and AI trust move in lockstep.
by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.
The figures break down as follows: restaurants at 97 percent, beauty at 94 percent, fitness and wellness at 93 percent, home services at 92 percent, and professional services at 84 percent.
For dining decisions, 78 percent of respondents favored written reviews compared with 59 percent for influencer recommendations, a 19-point gap.
For service professionals, the gap held at a similar magnitude: 81 percent favored written reviews against 61 percent for influencer picks.

According to Yelp, 77 percent of respondents said they trust platforms with detailed written reviews over those offering only star or numerical ratings when researching services, and 76 percent said the same held true for restaurants.
According to Yelp, 78 percent of respondents reported spending money on takeout or delivery in the past month, and 72 percent reported dining out in person over the same period.

Spending in both categories is also increasing year over year: 45 percent of respondents said they are spending more on takeout or delivery than a year earlier, and 45 percent said the same for dining out at restaurants.

When asked how they would allocate a bonus or a gift, 74 percent of respondents said they would put it toward dining out, and 70 percent said they would spend it on takeout or delivery, according to the survey.
According to Yelp, the menu itself was the most influential factor at 89 percent, followed closely by price at 87 percent.
Ambiance, by comparison, registered at 73 percent, a meaningful gap that the survey's authors linked to a persistent high-inflation environment.
According to the survey, 85 percent of respondents said price was influential when choosing a service professional such as a hair stylist or a pet groomer.

Beyond price, 81 percent cited up-to-date business information as a key factor, and 80 percent pointed to ease of booking, a combination the survey's authors said reflects an expectation for instant, low-friction access to information.
Both numbers sit well below the 76 to 81 percent range recorded for trust in detailed written reviews across the same categories.

That earlier study, published April 14, 2026 and reported by PPC Land at the time, surveyed 2,202 U.S. adults and found that just 15 percent of respondents overall said they trust AI search platforms "a lot," even though 65 percent had used one within the prior six months.

That earlier survey also found that 72 percent of respondents wanted AI platforms to always disclose where their information originates, and 69 percent wanted the option to leave an AI platform to visit a trusted source directly.

A YouTube creator marketing study conducted with Kantar and published through Think with Google found that 79 percent of Gen Z viewers said they trust recommendations from creators, a figure that sits closer to the written-review trust levels in Yelp's data than to the AI-summary figures, suggesting the trust gap runs specifically along a human-versus-machine axis rather than a broader skepticism toward all forms of online recommendation.
That report noted Yelp Host had fielded more than 1 million calls since its October 2025 launch, growing at an average of 38 percent month over month.
Usage of AI search tools was already at 65 percent among U.S. adults as of that earlier survey.

Operating profit was 40.6 billion U.S. dollars, up 18% from 34.4 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, keeping pace with the revenue growth rate, indicating no dilution of the profitability of core businesses.
Net profit was 35.8 billion U.S. dollars, compared with 27.2 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, representing a year-on-year increase of 31%.
LSEG analysts generally expected 4.24 U.S. dollars in diluted EPS and 31.5 billion U.S. dollars in net profit, meaning the actual performance fully beat market expectations.

The company recorded a 3.2 billion U.S. dollar gain from its investment in Anthropic, and expenses related to the voluntary separation program were lower than the forward guidance previously provided by the company on April 29, 2026, which was partially offset by severance pay and impairment charges in the Xbox division.

Excluding the impact of the OpenAI investment, on a Non-GAAP basis, Microsoft's net profit was 35.3 billion U.S. dollars, up 22% from 28.8 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year; diluted earnings per share was 4.74 U.S. dollars, up 23% year-on-year.

The difference between GAAP and Non-GAAP in the fourth fiscal quarter was a net loss of 480 million U.S. dollars caused by the OpenAI investment, while the investment generated a net gain of 1.575 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, with a net impact change of 2.055 billion U.S. dollars.

For the full fiscal year 2026, Microsoft's total revenue reached 331.8 billion U.S. dollars, up 18% year-on-year, and 16% growth in constant currency; operating profit was 155.2 billion U.S. dollars, up 21% year-on-year, and 19% growth in constant currency; net profit was 133.7 billion U.S. dollars, up 31% year-on-year; diluted earnings per share was 17.95 U.S. dollars, up 32% year-on-year.
In the fourth fiscal quarter, Microsoft returned 10.2 billion U.S. dollars to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

01 Azure's annual revenue exceeds 100 billion U.S. dollars for the first time Financial performance of Microsoft's three major business segments Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud division generated revenue of 39.3 billion U.S. dollars in the fourth fiscal quarter, compared with about 29.9 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, representing a year-on-year increase of 32% and 31% growth in constant currency, exceeding the general expectation of 38.16 billion U.S. dollars from analysts surveyed by StreetAccount.

This performance significantly exceeded Microsoft's previous guidance range of 39% to 40% in constant currency, and was also higher than the 39.6% expected by analysts surveyed by CNBC and StreetAccount.
The actual 43% growth rate directly eliminated this risk.
Satya Nadella, Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft, disclosed in the financial report that Azure's full-year revenue for fiscal 2026 exceeded 100 billion U.S. dollars for the first time.

Azure's 43% growth rate at its current volume means an annual increment of more than 40 billion U.S. dollars, and its absolute growth value is equivalent to the total revenue of some mid-sized cloud vendors.
Microsoft's remaining commercial performance obligations reached 6.78 trillion U.S. dollars at the end of the fourth fiscal quarter, up 84% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter.

Microsoft disclosed in January 2026 that about 45% of its then 6.25 trillion U.S. dollars of remaining commercial performance obligations were related to OpenAI, and the growth of commitments from non-OpenAI customers this quarter is diluting this concentration.

The overall revenue of Microsoft's cloud business in the fourth fiscal quarter was 59.3 billion U.S. dollars, up 27% year-on-year, covering Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial cloud, Dynamics 365, LinkedIn and other commercial cloud services.

Amy Hood, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Microsoft, said in the financial report: "We closed the fiscal year with strong performance, highlighted by Microsoft Cloud revenue of 59.3 billion U.S. dollars, up 27% year-on-year."

Microsoft's Productivity and Business Processes division recorded revenue of 37.8 billion U.S. dollars in the fourth fiscal quarter, up 14% year-on-year, exceeding the general expectation of 37.19 billion U.S. dollars from analysts surveyed by StreetAccount.
The number of paid seats for Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30 million.
Three months ago, Microsoft disclosed that this figure was about 20 million, representing a quarter-on-quarter increase of about 50%.
Brad Reback, an analyst at Stifel, previously predicted that this number would be 26 million, and the actual figure far exceeded expectations.
Revenue from Microsoft 365 commercial cloud increased by 14% on a reported basis, and 16% after adjustment.
Revenue from Microsoft 365 consumer cloud increased by 24%, and 22% in constant currency, showing that cloud service subscriptions on the individual user side also maintain robust growth.
Revenue from LinkedIn increased by 12%, and 10% in constant currency.
Revenue from Dynamics 365 increased by 13%, and 12% in constant currency, with stable demand for enterprise resource planning and customer relationship management software.

According to the financial report, Microsoft's revenue in the fourth fiscal quarter reached 90 billion U.S. dollars, up 18% from 76.4 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, and 17% growth in constant currency, which exceeded the general expectation of 87.62 billion U.S. dollars from analysts surveyed by the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG). Revenue from Azure and other cloud services increased by 43% this quarter, compared with a 40% growth rate in the previous quarter, accelerating by 3 percentage points, marking the fastest quarterly growth rate since the beginning of 2022. This year, Azure's revenue exceeded 100 billion U.S. dollars for the first time, and the number of paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats surpassed 30 million, which reflects customers' trust in our ability to help them with AI transformation."

The number of paid seats for Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30 million.
Three months ago, Microsoft disclosed that this figure was about 20 million, representing a quarter-on-quarter increase of about 50%.
Brad Reback, an analyst at Stifel, previously predicted that this number would be 26 million, and the actual figure far exceeded expectations.
Revenue from Microsoft 365 commercial cloud increased by 14% on a reported basis, and 16% after adjustment.
Revenue from Microsoft 365 consumer cloud increased by 24%, and 22% in constant currency, showing that cloud service subscriptions on the individual user side also maintain robust growth.
Revenue from LinkedIn increased by 12%, and 10% in constant currency.
Revenue from Dynamics 365 increased by 13%, and 12% in constant currency, with stable demand for enterprise resource planning and customer relationship management software.

This year, Azure's revenue exceeded 100 billion U.S. dollars for the first time, and the number of paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats surpassed 30 million, which reflects customers' trust in our ability to help them with AI transformation."

sourceContent.headline: PulseAI Research Reveals AI Becoming Trusted Daily Companion
sourceContent.description: PulseAI Research finds young Indians increasingly trust AI for learning, careers, decisions, and everyday productivity.
paragraphs: Trusted by many brands across FMCG, beauty, retail, and emerging consumer categories, PulseAI Research powers product innovation, campaign effectiveness, and growth strategy decisions.

Instead, it is becoming embedded across everyday life, from education and research to career planning, personal decisions, and information discovery, reflecting a broader behavioral shift in how consumers engage with technology.

The report also reflects PulseAI Research’s AI-led approach to decoding consumer behavior, combining AI-powered research capabilities with real-time consumer intelligence to help brands understand emerging trends faster and at greater depth.

Titled The AI Companion Report: How Young Indians Are Learning, Working, and Making Decisions with AI , the study surveyed over 2000 respondents across India and reveals that AI is no longer confined to workplace productivity or information retrieval.
More than 70% of respondents said they have already used AI for career advice, while over half have turned to it for travel planning, fitness advice, and personal decision-making.

Looking ahead, 62% said they would be comfortable using AI for career coaching, 56.9% for health guidance, and 54.5% for financial planning, signaling growing acceptance of AI in advisory roles traditionally occupied by people.
Nearly 30% of respondents said they use AI mainly for studying and learning, followed by research and information gathering ( 22.3% ).
Users are also increasingly comfortable delegating cognitively demanding tasks to AI, with research ( 29.6% ) and creative ideation ( 29.4% ) emerging as the two most commonly delegated activities.
Nearly 47% of respondents said their daily lives would be moderately or significantly disrupted if AI became unavailable for just one week.

paragraphs: The survey also showed that eight in 10 consumers are likely to rely on generative AI for up to half of their spending decisions, while 68 percent want AI agents to shop in ways that align with personal goals such as healthier lifestyles, sticking to budgets or making more intentional purchases.

CONSUMERS across Asia-Pacific are increasingly willing to let artificial intelligence (AI) agents make purchasing decisions on their behalf, signaling a major shift in retail and forcing brands to rethink how they attract and retain customers, according to a new survey by Accenture.

“Organizations will need to undertake an enterprise-wide reinvention,” he said, citing the need to integrate marketing, sales, service, operations and technology while strengthening AI governance and capabilities.

Accenture’s 2026 Consumer Pulse Survey found that more than one in four consumers now use large language models as their primary product discovery channel, while nine in 10 respondents said they would like to shop directly within generative AI tools.

The survey covered 25,590 consumers across 16 countries, including more than 7,000 respondents from Australia, Greater China, India and Japan.

sourceContent.headline: More Americans think China is world leader in AI, new survey reveals
sourceContent.description: Findings come as AI race between Washington and Beijing ramps up and with technology high on agenda at planned Trump-Xi summit in September.
paragraphs: More Americans think China is world leader in AI, new survey reveals    South China Morning Post
Findings come as AI race between Washington and Beijing ramps up and with technology high on agenda at planned Trump-Xi summit in September

The findings come against the backdrop of an accelerating AI race between Washington and Beijing, underscoring anxieties in the US that China is quickly eroding America’s technological edge by leveraging the capabilities of its top companies and gaining access to restricted advanced semiconductor chips.

“We’re leading China. We want to keep it that way. President Xi is coming over on September 24th, and we talked about it when I was over in Beijing, and we’ll be talking about it again,” said Trump, claiming Xi was impressed with the US’ advances in AI.
sourceContent.text:
More Americans think China is world leader in AI, new survey reveals    South China Morning Post

Findings come as AI race between Washington and Beijing ramps up and with technology high on agenda at planned Trump-Xi summit in September

The findings come against the backdrop of an accelerating AI race between Washington and Beijing, underscoring anxieties in the US that China is quickly eroding America’s technological edge by leveraging the capabilities of its top companies and gaining access to restricted advanced semiconductor chips.

“We’re leading China. We want to keep it that way. President Xi is coming over on September 24th, and we talked about it when I was over in Beijing, and we’ll be talking about it again,” said Trump, claiming Xi was impressed with the US’ advances in AI.

They largely see the proliferation of AI as an accelerant, not a threat, expecting it to free up more time, improve output, open new paths for growth, and create new opportunities for entry-level workers—but many also feel that they are adapting to AI faster than their organizations.

sourceContent.description: On the same earnings release day, tech giants Microsoft and Meta unveiled their latest financial results, triggering mixed market reactions as some metrics exceeded Wall Street’s consensus forecasts while other key performance indicators fell short of investor expectations, creating a split landscape of satisfaction and disappointment across stakeholders tracking the two leading tech firms’ quarterly operational and revenue outcomes.

Meta's total costs and expenses for the quarter reached $42 billion, up 55% year over year; operating profit dropped 8% to $18.78 billion, with the operating margin falling from 43% a year earlier to 31%; net profit decreased 14% to $15.85 billion, and earnings per share came in at $6.18, which fell below market expectations.
Microsoft & Meta Unveil Q2 2025 Financial Reports on Same Day: Zuckerberg’s Meta Spent Heavily on Metaverse Leaving Only $784M Cash Flow, Nadella’s Azure Drives Microsoft’s Stellar Huge Profits
Meta's revenue in the second quarter reached $60.8 billion, up 28% year over year, making it one of the fastest-growing quarters in recent years.

Microsoft's Confidence: AI Is No Longer Just an Expense Microsoft's revenue in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 reached $90 billion, up 18% year over year; operating profit was $40.6 billion, and net profit was $35.8 billion, up 31% year over year.
It should be noted that the net profit includes a $3.2 billion gain related to its investment in Anthropic.

But after excluding investments and one-off items, Microsoft's adjusted net profit still increased by 22% year over year, with revenue, profit and earnings per share all exceeding the company's previous guidance.
What truly excited the market was not the total revenue, but Microsoft's first disclosure that Azure's full-year revenue had exceeded $100 billion.

In this quarter, revenue from Azure and other cloud services rose 43%, beating market expectations; Microsoft also forecasts that Azure will grow by approximately 45% at constant currencies in the next quarter.
Microsoft Cloud's revenue for the quarter reached $59.3 billion, up 27% year over year, and its remaining commercial performance obligations rose to $6.78 trillion, up 84% year over year.
More critically, Microsoft stated that the approximately $500 billion in new contract commitments added this quarter all came from customers outside the top US foundational model companies.
The number of paid seats for Microsoft 365 Copilot also grew from 20 million in the previous quarter to more than 30 million, higher than the 26.9 million expected by analysts.

Microsoft Foundry has reached 100,000 customers, with revenue more than doubling year over year; two months after the launch of Agent 365, nearly 40 million Agents have been registered across tens of thousands of enterprises.

Microsoft's capital expenditure for the quarter reached $41 billion, up more than 70% year over year, while free cash flow fell 23% year over year to $19.6 billion.
In the next quarter, Microsoft expects capital expenditure to reach approximately $50 billion.

records.title: ChatFeatured Raises $2M to Build an Autonomous AI Search Agent for Marketing Teams

values.label: 조달액 · 2026
values.sourceLine: ChatFeatured, an AI search optimization platform, closed an oversubscribed $2 million pre-seed round led by Storytime Capital with participation from Garage Capital and BY Venture Partners, expanded from an original $1.5 million target after investor demand The company, founded in Toronto in January 2026 by Farris Nasr and Nithiiyan Skhanthan, helps marketing teams analyze what large language models cite, identify competitor gaps, and build, publish, and track content to improve AI search visibility Funding will support team growth, go-to-market expansion, and an autonomous answer engine optimization agent; ChatFeatured now serves customers across the US, Canada, Australia, the UK, and Germany, growing more than 40 percent month-over-month PRESS RELEASE — ChatFeatured, the AI search optimization platform that helps marketing teams turn visibility data into published content and measurable results, has announced an oversubscribed USD $2 million pre-seed round.

sourceContent.headline: AI Governance in Banking | Managing AI Risks and Scaling Responsible AI Adoption
sourceContent.description: Banks are accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, from generative AI applications to more advanced autonomous AI systems. However, many financial institutions are finding that their AI governance frameworks are not evolving at the same pace as AI capabilities. Strengthening AI governance is becoming essential to manage risks, meet regulatory expectations and enable responsible AI scaling.
paragraphs: Danish banks have an opportunity to lead in responsible AI adoption by embedding governance excellence from the outset, rather than retrofitting controls as risks emerge.
AI Adoption is accelerating, but AI governance maturity is lagging: 63% of bank employees use AI weekly; 87% of banks could significantly improve governance and only 13% reach leading maturity.
Strengthening AI governance is becoming essential to manage risks, meet regulatory expectations and enable responsible AI scaling.

sourceContent.headline: How do Canadians feel about using AI work?
sourceContent.description: Learn how the 2026 TD AI Insights Report helps reveal Canadians’ attitudes towards AI in the workplace.
paragraphs: According to the survey results, nearly 80% of respondents said AI adoption in the workplace is inevitable.

So far in fiscal 2026 (or since November 1, 2025 until July 31, 2026) calls to second-level support have gone down almost 30%, which means more colleagues are getting the answers they need, right when they need them.
At the Bank, 98% of those with Microsoft Copilot are active users (used within the past two weeks), with an average daily adoption rate of 51%.
Most respondents (75%) rated their AI skill level as a “C” or lower, with only 4% giving themselves an A.

고려대학교와 연세대는 NC AI와 Gabia가 제공하는 산업 구축 경험과 함께 필요한 학문적 AI 및 컴퓨터 과학 연구 역량을 제공함

sourceContent.description: France finds OpenAI, Google and Anthropic hold 84% of the AI agent market. What the advisory opinion means for competition and Australia.
paragraphs: The core finding: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic together control 84% of the AI agent market, based on usage data the authority cites from Sensor Tower.

The length reflects how broadly the authority interpreted its brief: not just chatbots, but the wider shift toward autonomous agents that can complete tasks like booking travel, comparing prices or filing paperwork without a human clicking through each step.

In an opinion published July 18, 2026, the Autorité de la concurrence found that OpenAI, Google and Anthropic together hold 84% of the AI agent market.
Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending will reach $2.52 trillion in 2026, with $452 billion of that going specifically to AI software.
A narrower Gartner estimate, focused specifically on AI platforms and models rather than the wider AI software category, puts that segment at $64 billion for 2026.
An 84% combined share leaves roughly 16% of the AI agent market split among everyone else, and that group has been anything but quiet in 2026.

sourceContent.headline: AI 보조 기능과 완전 자율 기능의 소비자 수용 격차
sourceContent.text:
NRI conducted a survey of 2,500 consumers across five major U.S. cities.

AI is widely welcomed when it supports drivers rather than takes control.

Americans are open to AI when it enhances human decisions, but hesitant when AI replaces them entirely.

64% of New York and 66% of Los Angeles respondents viewed AI-powered predictive maintenance positively.

Only 39% of New York and 47% of Los Angeles respondents felt positive about fully autonomous driving.
